blocks.text: Overview

This article tracks recent additions and changes to AP Smart Link, the in-shop terminal that shops use to receive orders, take payments and manage day-to-day trading. Use this as a quick reference when a shop calls in asking 'what changed' or 'why does my terminal look different'. Staff should check this page before escalating a ticket about a UI change, since most cosmetic differences are intentional rollout changes rather than faults.

Smart Link updates are pushed over-the-air (OTA) to terminals in batches, usually overnight between 2am and 5am UK time, so shops will typically see new features appear when they open the following morning. Larger changes are staged: they may go to a small percentage of terminals first (a 'ring 1' rollout) before going wide, so two shops on the same street can legitimately be on different versions for a few days.
Recent changes

items: Order acceptance countdown timer increased from 60 seconds to 90 seconds by default, configurable down to 45 seconds under Settings > Orders > Acceptance Window.
[[tap-to-pay-getting-started|Tap to Pay]] card reader pairing moved from a Bluetooth-only flow to also support USB-C tethering for shops with weak in-store Wi-Fi.
My Orders notification sound can now be set separately from the general alert tone, under Settings > Notifications > Order Sounds.
The [[hw-smart-link-tracking-drivers|driver tracking map]] now shows estimated return-to-shop time, not just delivery ETA.
[[menu-availability|Menu Availability]] toggles (products, variants, categories) now sync to the customer-facing site within roughly 10 seconds, down from up to 2 minutes previously.
[[request-funds-same-day|Request Funds]] same-day option added directly to the [[sales-ap-funds|AP Funds]] tile on the terminal home screen instead of being buried in the Payouts menu.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the Smart Link terminal home screen showing the redesigned AP Funds tile with the new same-day Request Funds shortcut in the top-right corner.

blocks.text: How shops find version information

The current firmware and app version is shown under Settings > About > Software Version. When troubleshooting, always ask the shop to read this number back, as some fixes only apply from a specific build onward (for example, the Tap to Pay USB-C fix only applies from build 4.12.0 onward). Shops running anything below 4.9.0 are considered out of support for new feature requests and should be advised to reboot the terminal, which usually triggers a pending update check (see [[hw-smart-link-firmware-updates|Managing Firmware Updates]] for the full process).

If a shop reports missing a feature described in this article, the most common cause is that the terminal has update checks disabled under Settings > System > Auto Update, which some shops turn off during busy trading periods to avoid a mid-service reboot. Advise them to re-enable this and manually trigger a check via Settings > System > Check for Updates.
Troubleshooting

If a shop says 'my terminal froze after the update', the standard first step is a full power-off (hold the power button 10 seconds) rather than a soft restart, since a soft restart can leave the update in a half-applied state. If the terminal boots to a black screen with a spinning dot for more than 5 minutes, log a hardware ticket rather than continuing to troubleshoot software.

A common complaint after an update is 'the buttons have moved', this is expected with UI refreshes and is not a fault. Reassure the shop and point them to the in-app 'What's New' banner, which they can dismiss but which reappears once per update.

If a shop reports that My Orders notifications have gone silent since an update, check whether Order Sounds was reset to 'Silent' during the update, this has happened on a small number of terminals migrating from pre-4.9.0 builds and is a known issue tracked internally; there is no shop-side fix beyond re-selecting a tone.
Overview

My Orders is the screen on Smart Link where incoming orders from the FMO app and website land in real time. It is the first thing most staff interact with during a shift, so understanding exactly how and when alerts fire is important when a shop calls in saying they 'missed an order'.

When a customer places an order, it appears on My Orders within 2-3 seconds under normal network conditions, accompanied by an audible alert and a flashing banner across the top of the screen. The order sits in a 'Pending' state until a staff member taps Accept or Decline.
How the alert behaves

items: The alert sound repeats every 8 seconds until the order is actioned, and increases in volume slightly on the third repeat.

If no action is taken within the Acceptance Window (default 90 seconds, configurable under Settings > Orders > Acceptance Window), the order auto-declines and the customer is notified and refunded automatically.
A red badge with the pending order count appears on the Smart Link home screen icon so staff can see queued orders from other screens.

[[pre-orders-how-they-work|Pre-Orders]] (orders placed for a future time slot) do not trigger the same urgent alert, they appear with a calendar icon and a softer chime, since they don't need immediate action.
If the shop is set to 'Closed' or 'Paused' in [[menu-availability|Menu Availability]], no new orders reach My Orders at all, so there is nothing to accept.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the My Orders screen showing a pending order card with the countdown timer, customer name, order total and Accept/Decline buttons.

blocks.text: Accepting, declining and editing

[[hw-smart-link-accept-decline|Accepting an order]] moves it to the 'Preparing' column and starts the prep timer shown on the order card. Declining requires a reason to be selected from a short list (Too Busy, Item Unavailable, Closing Soon, Other) which is logged against the shop for reporting purposes, a high decline rate can trigger an account review. Staff can also use Edit Order from within an accepted order card if the customer needs a change made after acceptance (see the separate [[edit-order-updating|Edit Order]] article for details).

Multiple staff can be logged into My Orders on different devices in larger shops (for example, a kitchen tablet and a front counter terminal); accepting on one device instantly removes the pending state on the other to avoid double-handling.
Common questions

'We didn't hear the order come in' is the most frequent call type related to this feature. First check the terminal isn't set to silent or on low volume, then check whether Do Not Disturb hours are configured under Settings > Notifications > Quiet Hours, some shops set this accidentally while trying to mute end-of-night testing.

'The order disappeared before we could accept it' usually means the Acceptance Window expired. Pull the order timestamp from the Orders History log and compare against the shop's configured window, if it's set unusually low (e.g. 45 seconds during a busy dinner rush) recommend increasing it.

If a shop reports orders appearing twice, this is almost always two staff logged into My Orders under the same account on different devices, causing a duplicate render rather than a duplicate order, check the order reference number is identical before escalating as a billing issue.
Overview

Request Funds lets a shop pull forward money sitting in their [[sales-ap-funds|AP Funds]] balance instead of waiting for the [[sales-getting-paid-timelines|standard payout cycle]]. The same-day option is the fastest route available and is commonly asked about by shops with cash-flow pressure, particularly around supplier payment days or after a busy weekend.

Standard bank transfers from AP Funds take 3-5 business days and are free. Same-day Request Funds transfers arrive the same working day when requested before the cutoff, but carry a flat processing fee, currently £2.50 per request regardless of amount.
How to submit a same-day request

items: On the Smart Link home screen, tap the AP Funds tile, then Request Funds.
Select 'Same Day' rather than 'Standard' from the transfer speed options.
Enter the amount, this cannot exceed the available AP Funds balance shown at the top of the screen, and there is a minimum request amount of £20.
Confirm the destination account, which is the bank account linked to the shop's [[sales-advantage-card|Advantage Card]] unless changed under Settings > Payouts > Bank Details.
Review the £2.50 fee shown on the confirmation screen and tap Confirm Request.

blocks.text: Cutoff times and processing

Same-day requests must be submitted before 2pm UK time on a business day to guarantee same-day arrival; requests submitted after 2pm are processed the next business day but the fee is still charged, since the request has already been queued. Requests submitted on a weekend or bank holiday are treated as next-business-day regardless of time.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the Request Funds confirmation screen showing the Same Day option selected, the £2.50 fee line item, and the estimated arrival time.

blocks.text: A shop can only have one same-day request in flight at a time. If a second request is attempted while one is processing, the terminal shows 'A request is already in progress' and blocks submission until the first clears.
Troubleshooting

'The money hasn't arrived and it's been same-day', first confirm the request was submitted before the 2pm cutoff by checking the timestamp under AP Funds > Request History. If it was submitted before cutoff and still hasn't landed by end of business day, this needs escalating to Payments Ops rather than resolved at first line, since it likely means the bank details on file are incorrect or the receiving bank has flagged the transfer.

'Why was I charged £2.50 when I selected Standard', this only happens if the shop switched from Same Day to Standard after already seeing the fee screen but the app cached the wrong state; ask the shop to check the Request History entry, and if it confirms Standard was selected, refund the fee as a goodwill gesture and log a bug report.

'Can I request more than my balance shows', no, the request amount is hard-capped at the visible AP Funds balance at the moment of request; pending card transactions from the last few hours may not have cleared into the balance yet, which explains why the available amount can look lower than the shop expects mid-shift.
Shops on the introductory 90-day trial period do not have access to same-day requests, only standard 3-5 day transfers, until the trial converts to a paid subscription.
Overview

Customer Numbers lets a shop store more than one contact number against a single customer profile in Smart Link. This is useful for households that order together but call from different phones, or for customers who order from a landline but need SMS delivery updates sent to a mobile.

Each customer profile can hold up to 5 numbers. One number must always be marked as Primary, this is the number used for automatic [[mkt-sms-delivery-notifications|delivery-status SMS notifications]] and any [[mkt-sms-sending-campaign|SMS marketing campaigns]] the shop sends, unless a different number is chosen for a specific order.
Adding a number

items: Open the customer's profile from Orders > Customers, or search by an existing number.
Tap Add Number, enter the new number, and select a label (Mobile, Home, Work, Other).
Optionally mark the new number as Primary, this replaces the previous primary but keeps the old number saved under the profile.
Save. The number is available for selection immediately on the next order taken for that customer.

blocks.text: Numbers can also be added mid-order: when a customer calls in and a staff member is taking a phone order, if the incoming caller ID doesn't match any saved number on the matched profile (matched by name or address), Smart Link prompts 'Add this number to [Customer Name]?' rather than creating a duplicate customer record.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of a customer profile page showing three saved numbers labelled Mobile (Primary), Home and Work, with the Add Number button beneath.

blocks.text: Where this matters elsewhere

[[text-to-pay-account-limits|Text to Pay]] always sends the payment link to whichever number is selected on the order being processed, not automatically the Primary number, so staff should double check the number shown before sending. [[my-orders-incoming|My Orders]] shows the number the order came in on next to the customer name, which helps staff spot when a call is coming from a non-primary saved number, e.g. a partner calling from a work phone.

Duplicate numbers cannot exist across two different customer profiles, if a staff member tries to add a number already saved elsewhere, Smart Link shows 'This number is already linked to [Name]' and offers to merge the profiles.
Common questions

'We can't delete an old number', a number cannot be removed if it's the only one left on a profile, or if it's tied to an order placed in the last 90 days (kept for dispute/refund reference). Staff should add a new number and mark it Primary before removing the old one.

'A customer says they're not getting delivery texts', check which number is marked Primary; if the customer usually orders from a second number that isn't Primary, notifications will silently go to the wrong phone. This is the single most common cause of 'my texts aren't arriving' complaints on this feature.

'Two customer profiles seem to be for the same person', this happens when a customer orders once by phone and once online using a different number before Customer Numbers links them; use the merge option from either profile's menu (三-dot menu > Merge Customer) rather than manually recreating orders.
Overview

Tap to Pay turns a compatible Smart Link terminal into a contactless card reader, letting shops take chip-and-PIN, contactless card and mobile wallet payments (Apple Pay, Google Pay) directly at the counter or door, with no separate card machine needed. Card takings collected this way flow straight into the shop's [[sales-ap-funds|AP Funds]] balance alongside online payments, and can be drawn on via the [[sales-advantage-card|Advantage Card]] or pulled out through [[request-funds-same-day|Request Funds]].
There is no transaction fee for Tap to Pay payments on FMO, this is covered under the shop's flat monthly subscription, consistent with FMO's 0% commission model.
Getting set up

items: Go to Settings > Payments > Tap to Pay on the Smart Link terminal.
Tap Enable Tap to Pay, this requires the shop's Advantage Card to be active, since Tap to Pay cannot be enabled on accounts still in manual bank verification.
Pair the reader: newer terminals (build 4.12.0+) support both Bluetooth and USB-C tethering; older terminals are Bluetooth-only.
Run a test transaction for £0.00 (a card check, not a real charge) to confirm the reader is communicating correctly.
Train staff on the two accepted methods: presenting a physical card/phone to the terminal's NFC area, or inserting a chip card for PIN entry as a fallback.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the Tap to Pay setup screen showing the pairing status, a green 'Reader Connected' indicator, and the Run Test Transaction button.

blocks.text: Taking a payment

From an active order on My Orders or a walk-in sale started from the terminal's New Sale screen, staff select Tap to Pay as the payment method, enter or confirm the amount, and hand the terminal to the customer (or turn it to face them). The screen shows 'Ready, Present Card' with a pulsing NFC icon. Payment confirms in under 3 seconds on a good connection and prints a receipt automatically if the shop has receipt printing enabled.

The [[mkt-minimum-discount|minimum 3% customer discount]] still applies to orders paid via Tap to Pay in-store when the order was placed through the FMO app or site (e.g. a click-and-collect order paid at the counter); walk-in sales rung up directly on the terminal without an online order are not eligible for the discount since there is no online order to discount.
Troubleshooting

'Card declined' with no further detail usually means an issuer-side decline (insufficient funds, bank fraud flag) rather than a terminal fault, advise the customer to try a different card or contact their bank; retrying the same card repeatedly on FMO's side won't help (see [[hw-smart-link-card-payments|Accepting Card Payments]] for the wider card-payments troubleshooting flow).

'Reader shows Disconnected', most commonly a Bluetooth pairing drop. First try toggling Bluetooth off and on under Settings > Payments > Tap to Pay > Reconnect Reader; if that fails, switch to a USB-C tether if the terminal supports it, since this is more reliable in shops with a lot of kitchen equipment causing Bluetooth interference.

'Customer says they were charged twice', check the Payments log for two entries with different reference numbers close together; this typically means the first tap failed silently (no confirmation shown) and staff retried without realising the first attempt actually went through. Refund the duplicate from Payments > Transaction History > Refund.

Tap to Pay is not currently available on terminals running firmware below 4.9.0, advise the shop to update via Settings > System > Check for Updates before attempting setup (see [[hw-smart-link-firmware-updates|Managing Firmware Updates]]).
Overview

Text to Pay lets a shop send a customer an SMS payment link for a phone or over-the-counter order instead of taking card details directly or requiring cash. It's commonly used for phone orders where the customer wants to pay by card but isn't collecting in person, or for pre-orders taken over the phone.

Because Text to Pay generates a live payment link tied to the shop's account, FMO applies account-level limits to reduce fraud risk and to control SMS costs, which are billed back to the shop above a monthly allowance.
Standard limits

items: Maximum single Text to Pay link value: £250. Larger orders must be split into multiple links or taken via [[tap-to-pay-getting-started|Tap to Pay]] in person.
Maximum of 40 outstanding (unpaid) Text to Pay links at any one time per shop.
A payment link expires 30 minutes after it is sent; expired links must be resent, they cannot be reactivated.

Included SMS allowance is 300 messages per month on the Standard plan (a separate allowance from the [[mkt-sms-sending-campaign|SMS marketing campaign]] allowance); each Text to Pay send counts as one message against this allowance.
Shops on the introductory 90-day trial are capped at £100 per link and 10 outstanding links, rising to standard limits once the account converts to a paid subscription.

blocks.text: Where to manage limits

Shop-level settings (link expiry within the allowed range, default message wording) are managed under Settings > Payments > Text to Pay. The hard account limits above (max value, max outstanding links, SMS allowance) are not editable by the shop directly, a shop requesting a higher limit, for example to send £400 catering order links, needs this raised via an account review, which checks trading history and [[acc-chargebacks|chargeback]] rate before approving.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the Text to Pay settings page showing the current outstanding link count (12 of 40), the SMS allowance usage bar, and the link expiry dropdown.

blocks.text: SMS usage beyond the monthly allowance is billed at £0.04 per message and appears as a line item on the shop's [[sales-vat-invoicing|next invoice]], viewable under Billing > Usage Charges.
Troubleshooting

'The link says expired but it's only been 10 minutes', check the customer's phone clock/timezone isn't the issue first, then check whether the shop resent the same order twice, since only the most recently sent link for an order stays active and earlier ones auto-expire immediately.

'We can't send any more Text to Pay links', check the outstanding link count under Settings > Payments > Text to Pay; if it's at 40, links need to be cleared by the customer paying or the shop manually cancelling stale ones under Payments > Pending Links > Cancel.

'Customer paid but the order still shows unpaid', there can be a short delay (up to 60 seconds) between payment confirmation and the order status updating; if it's been longer than that, check Payments > Transaction History for the payment reference before assuming the payment failed.
A shop asking to raise their £250 per-link cap for a specific large order should be advised this isn't instant, flag it to Account Management rather than promising a same-day increase.
Overview

Pre-Orders let customers place an order in advance for a future collection or delivery time, rather than for immediate fulfilment. This is used heavily around events (e.g. a big match night) and by shops that want to smooth out demand ahead of a known busy period.

Pre-Orders appear on My Orders with a calendar icon and a scheduled time rather than the usual 'now' order flow, and they do not count against the standard Acceptance Window countdown, since there's no urgency to accept them immediately.
Enabling Pre-Orders

items: Go to Settings > Orders > Pre-Orders and toggle Enable Pre-Orders on.
Set the booking window, how far in advance customers can order, e.g. up to 7 days ahead (shop-configurable, max 14 days).
Set the minimum lead time, how close to the requested slot a customer can still book, default 45 minutes.
Configure slot capacity if the shop wants to cap how many Pre-Orders can land in the same 15-minute slot, to avoid a kitchen bottleneck.
Save, Pre-Orders become bookable on the customer-facing site within a few minutes.

blocks.text: How shops handle them day to day

Pre-Orders sit in a separate 'Upcoming' tab on [[my-orders-incoming|My Orders]] until they move into the active order queue automatically at a configurable point before the requested time (default 30 minutes prior), at which point they behave like a normal order requiring Accept/Decline within the standard window.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the My Orders Upcoming tab listing three Pre-Orders with their scheduled collection times, sorted earliest first.

blocks.text: Staff can still use [[edit-order-updating|Edit Order]] and [[menu-availability|Menu Availability]] changes against a Pre-Order before it activates, for example, if an item sells out later that day, the shop can edit an existing Pre-Order that included it and the customer is notified of the change by [[mkt-sms-delivery-notifications|SMS]] if [[text-to-pay-account-limits|Text to Pay]]/notifications are enabled.

Payment for a Pre-Order is taken at the time of booking, not at collection/delivery time, so a declined Pre-Order (e.g. because the shop is unexpectedly closing early) triggers an automatic refund the same way a declined immediate order does.
Troubleshooting

'Customer says they couldn't book a slot', check the booking window and minimum lead time settings; a common cause is a shop setting the lead time too high (e.g. 3 hours) without realising it blocks same-evening bookings.

'A Pre-Order never moved into the active queue', check Settings > Orders > Pre-Orders for the 'activate before' setting; if it's misconfigured to a very small window (e.g. 2 minutes) staff can easily miss it moving over. Recommend the default 30 minutes for most shops.

'We're getting too many Pre-Orders for one time slot', this means Slot Capacity isn't set; walk the shop through Settings > Orders > Pre-Orders > Slot Capacity and suggest a starting cap based on their average items-per-order and kitchen throughput.
Overview

Edit Order lets shop staff make changes to a customer's order after it has already been placed and, in most cases, after it has been accepted, for example, swapping an out-of-stock item, correcting a delivery address typo, or adjusting quantities the customer phones in to change.

Edit Order is accessed from the order detail screen (tap into any order from [[my-orders-incoming|My Orders]] or Orders History) via the Edit Order button. Not every field is editable at every stage, what can change depends on the order's current status.
What can be edited, and when

items: Pending orders: any field can be edited freely, including items, quantities, delivery/collection choice and address.

Accepted / Preparing orders: items and quantities can still be changed, but the delivery address is locked once a driver has been assigned in the [[hw-smart-link-tracking-drivers|Driver Tracking]] screen.
Out for Delivery orders: only minor changes are allowed (e.g. adding a note for the driver); item and price changes are blocked to prevent disputes mid-delivery.
Completed orders: no live edit is possible; corrections must go through a manual refund or adjustment instead, logged under Payments > Adjustments.

blocks.text: Any edit that changes the order total triggers an automatic recalculation of the customer's discount and, where relevant, the payment already taken. If the new total is higher, Smart Link attempts to take an additional payment automatically via the original payment method (or prompts for [[tap-to-pay-getting-started|Tap to Pay]]/[[text-to-pay-account-limits|Text to Pay]] if that fails); if lower, the difference is refunded automatically, usually within a few minutes.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the Edit Order screen showing an item being swapped, with the recalculated order total and discount shown at the bottom before confirming.

blocks.text: Notifications to the customer

Every confirmed edit sends the customer an automatic SMS/app notification summarising what changed, using the same [[mkt-sms-delivery-notifications|delivery-status notification]] system referenced elsewhere in Smart Link. Staff should still call the customer directly for anything substantial (e.g. an item substitution) rather than relying on the notification alone, since not all customers have notifications enabled.
Troubleshooting

'Edit Order button is greyed out', this almost always means the order has moved to Out for Delivery or Completed status; check the order status badge at the top of the order detail screen before assuming it's a fault.

'We changed an item but the customer wasn't charged the difference', check Payments > Transaction History for a failed automatic charge attempt; if the customer's card was declined for the top-up amount, the edit still saves but the balance sits as 'Outstanding' and needs collecting manually, usually via a fresh Text to Pay link.

'Customer disputes an edit they didn't agree to', pull the Edit Order audit log from the order detail screen (三-dot menu > Edit History), which timestamps every change and the staff account that made it, before responding to the dispute.

A frequent question from new starters is whether Edit Order can be used to apply a discretionary discount, it cannot; discretionary discounts are a separate function under Payments > Manual Adjustment and are not part of Edit Order.
Overview

Menu Availability controls what customers can actually order at any given moment, at three levels: individual products, variants (sizes, flavours, crust types etc.), and whole categories. Getting this right prevents the most common cause of order cancellations, a customer ordering something the kitchen has already run out of.

Availability changes made on Smart Link sync to the live customer-facing menu within roughly 10 seconds (as of the [[whats-new-in-smartlink|latest Smart Link update]]), so staff should get comfortable making changes mid-service rather than waiting for a quiet moment.
The three levels

items: Product level: turning off a whole dish (e.g. 'Chicken Tikka Masala') removes it from the menu entirely until re-enabled.
Variant level: turning off a specific option within a product (e.g. the 'Large' size of a pizza, or 'Stuffed Crust') while leaving other sizes/options available.

Category level: turning off an entire category (e.g. 'Desserts') hides every item within it, useful when a section of the kitchen is down (broken fryer, freezer issue) rather than toggling items one by one.

blocks.text: Making changes

From Settings > Menu > Availability, staff can search for a product or variant by name and toggle it off with a single tap. There's also a bulk 86 mode (industry slang for 'sold out') accessible from the same screen, which lets staff select multiple items across categories and disable them in one action, handy at close of service when several ingredients have run low.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the Menu Availability screen showing a product list with toggle switches, one variant expanded to show its individual size options, and the bulk 86 mode selection bar at the bottom.

blocks.text: Availability toggles can be scheduled rather than manual, for example, a shop can set 'Sunday Roast' to only ever be available Sundays 12pm-4pm under the item's Advanced Availability settings, and it will automatically hide outside that window without staff needing to remember.
Interaction with orders

If an item is disabled after a customer has already added it to their basket but before they check out, checkout will block with 'This item is no longer available' and ask them to remove it. If a [[pre-orders-how-they-work|Pre-Order]] was placed earlier including an item that later becomes unavailable, staff need to use [[edit-order-updating|Edit Order]] to substitute or remove it manually, disabling availability does not retroactively change existing orders.
Troubleshooting

'We turned an item off but customers can still order it', check whether the item exists in more than one category (some shops list the same dish under both a 'Chef's Specials' and a regional category); disabling it in one place doesn't disable the other listing, each needs toggling separately unless it's genuinely the same product record.

'A whole category disappeared and we don't know why', check Advanced Availability scheduling on the category; a staff member may have set a time-limited window (e.g. lunch-only) without realising it would auto-hide outside those hours.

'Customer ordered a size we don't do anymore', this points to a variant not being fully removed; check under the product's Variants tab rather than just the top-level product toggle, since disabling the base product doesn't automatically disable variants if the product itself is still technically active for other variants.

As general guidance for phone support: always ask the shop to confirm they're looking at Settings > Menu > Availability specifically, since some shops confuse this with the separate Menu Editor (which changes prices and descriptions, not live availability).
Overview

AP Smart Link (also referred to simply as 'the terminal') is the in-shop hardware device that every FMO partner shop uses to run day-to-day online ordering. It is a countertop unit combining an order screen, a built-in thermal receipt printer, and a card payment reader in a single box. When a customer places an order through the FMO app or website, it arrives on the terminal in real time, prints automatically, and the shop accepts or declines it directly on the screen.

The terminal is the central hub for the shop's FMO account: it handles order intake, card and contactless payments at no transaction fee, driver tracking for deliveries, and access to AP Funds, the shop's instant online takings balance. Shops do not need a separate card machine, a separate printer, or a separate tracking app, Smart Link replaces all three.
What's in the box

items: AP Smart Link terminal unit (model SL-200)
Countertop stand / charging cradle
UK 3-pin mains power adapter (12V, 3A)
Ethernet cable (2m, Cat5e)
One starter roll of 80mm thermal receipt paper
Quick-start card insert and terminal ID sticker

blocks.caption: AP Smart Link terminal on its countertop stand, showing the order screen, built-in printer lid, and card reader slot on the right edge.

blocks.text: Pre-configuration and first power-on

Every Smart Link terminal is shipped pre-configured to the specific shop it's assigned to, the shop's menu, opening hours, delivery zones, and payment settings are already loaded onto the device before it leaves the warehouse. Staff do not need to manually pair the terminal to the shop's FMO account. On first power-on, the terminal will display the shop name and address on the home screen within roughly 60 seconds; if it instead shows a 'Terminal Not Registered' message, the unit was not provisioned correctly and needs replacing via the Hardware team, not reconfiguring on-site.

To get the terminal running for the first time: connect the power adapter, connect either Wi-Fi (via Settings > Network > Wi-Fi) or the supplied ethernet cable, and wait for the home screen to show a green Wi-Fi/signal icon in the top right corner. The terminal will pull down its shop profile automatically and is ready to take live orders once the icon turns solid green.
Everyday use in shop

items: Incoming orders appear on screen and print automatically on the [[hw-smart-link-printing-receipts|built-in printer]]
Staff tap [[hw-smart-link-accept-decline|Accept or Decline]] within the order's response window
Card and contactless payments for counter/collection orders are taken directly on the [[hw-smart-link-card-payments|terminal reader]]
Delivery orders show [[hw-smart-link-tracking-drivers|live driver status]] once a driver is assigned
The [[sales-ap-funds|AP Funds]] balance and [[sales-advantage-card|Advantage Card]] details are accessible from the Payments menu

blocks.text: Common issues

Screen unresponsive after power-on: hold the power button on the top edge for 10 seconds to force a restart. If the FMO logo hangs on screen for more than 2 minutes, this indicates a firmware update stalled, leave it connected to power and Wi-Fi and it will typically resolve within 15 minutes.
Home screen shows the wrong shop name or old menu items: this usually means a profile sync didn't complete. Go to Settings > Account > Sync Now to force a refresh rather than restarting the unit.

Terminal shows 'Terminal Not Registered': this is a provisioning fault, not a network issue, do not attempt to re-pair it in shop. Log a hardware ticket with the terminal's serial number (printed on the underside sticker) so a replacement or remote re-provision can be arranged.
Overview

AP Smart Link includes a built-in card reader that accepts chip and PIN, contactless card, and digital wallet payments (Apple Pay, Google Pay) for counter and collection orders. Unlike a standalone card machine, there is no per-transaction fee charged to the shop, card acceptance is included as part of the flat monthly Smart Link subscription. This applies to in-store payments taken on the terminal itself; online payments taken through the app or website at checkout are settled separately into [[sales-ap-funds|AP Funds]].
Taking a payment

items: From the order screen, tap Take Payment on the relevant order, or tap New Sale for a walk-in customer
Confirm the amount shown matches the till total
Present the card or device to the reader panel on the right edge of the terminal, or insert a chip card into the slot beneath it
For chip and PIN, the customer enters their PIN on the terminal's on-screen keypad
Wait for the green tick and 'Approved' message before releasing the card

blocks.caption: Close-up of the card reader panel showing the contactless tap zone and chip insert slot on the right-hand edge of the terminal.

blocks.text: Contactless and digital wallets

Contactless taps (card, phone, or watch) are read from the marked zone above the chip slot, a short vibration and single beep confirm the tap was registered. Contactless payments above £100 will prompt for chip and PIN as a security step; this limit is set by the card networks, not configurable in shop. Digital wallet payments (Apple Pay, Google Pay) behave identically to a contactless card tap and use the same zone.
Refunds and voids

A payment can be voided within the same session if the customer's card is still present and the transaction hasn't been finalised, tap Cancel before the 'Approved' screen appears. Once a transaction is finalised, it must be processed as a refund from Payments > Transaction History > select transaction > Refund. Refunds typically appear back on the customer's card within 3-5 business days, in line with standard card scheme timelines.
Where payments go

Card takings, whether taken in shop on the terminal or online through the app, are added to the shop's [[sales-ap-funds|AP Funds]] balance. Funds can be accessed instantly using the [[sales-advantage-card|Advantage Card]], [[sales-getting-paid-timelines|transferred to a bank account]] (3-5 business days standard, or same-day for a small transfer fee), or left in the AP Funds balance. The terminal's Payments menu shows a running total of the day's card takings alongside cash orders marked as paid.
Troubleshooting

Card declined with message 'Not Authorised': this is an issuing bank decline, not a terminal fault, ask the customer to try a different card or contact their bank. Repeated declines across different cards in a short period can indicate the terminal's payment module needs a restart from Settings > Hardware > Payment Module > Restart.

Reader not detecting taps or chip cards: check the small LED beside the chip slot, solid blue means ready, no light means the payment module has dropped connection and needs the restart above, flashing red means a card fault (try a different card first).

Transaction stuck on 'Processing' for more than 30 seconds: do not tap again. Wait for it to time out (60 seconds) and either succeed or show 'Failed' before retaking the payment, to avoid a duplicate charge.

PIN pad unresponsive to touch: this is usually a screen calibration issue after a drop or knock. Log a hardware ticket, do not attempt to recalibrate manually, as PIN entry components are tamper-sealed for PCI compliance.
Overview

[[hw-smart-link-getting-started|AP Smart Link]] has a built-in 80mm thermal printer that automatically prints a receipt for every incoming order the moment it's [[hw-smart-link-accept-decline|accepted]]. This gives kitchen and delivery staff a physical ticket showing the order items, customisations, customer name, delivery/collection details, and payment status, without needing to manually type or copy anything from the screen.
How automatic printing works

When an order is accepted (either manually or via auto-accept if enabled), the terminal sends the ticket to the internal print engine within 2-3 seconds. Two tickets print by default: a kitchen copy (items and customisations only) and a customer/delivery copy (includes address and payment status). This can be changed to a single combined ticket via Settings > Hardware > Printer > Ticket Layout.

items: Kitchen copy: item names, quantities, customisations, allergen flags, order number
Delivery copy: customer name, address, phone number, payment status (Paid Online / Pay on Delivery), order number
Both copies print with a barcode at the bottom used for the [[my-orders-incoming|My Orders]] lookup

blocks.caption: Printer paper compartment open, showing the 80mm thermal roll loaded with the paper feeding from underneath and the cutter bar along the top edge.

blocks.text: Paper and maintenance

The terminal takes standard 80mm x 60mm thermal paper rolls, BPA-free, available from the FMO hardware store or any compatible thermal till roll supplier. To replace the roll: lift the printer compartment latch on the top rear of the unit, remove the spent core, drop in the new roll with the paper feeding from underneath (printed side facing down), and close the lid until it clicks. Do not pull paper backwards through the printer as this can damage the thermal head.
Reprinting a ticket

If a ticket needs reprinting (smudged, torn, or accidentally binned), go to Orders > Order History, select the order, and tap Reprint. Reprinted tickets are marked with a 'REPRINT' watermark across the top so kitchen staff don't confuse them with duplicate new orders.
Troubleshooting

Order appears on screen but nothing prints: first rule out a [[hw-smart-link-connectivity|connectivity]] drop, then check the printer status icon at the top of the screen. A grey printer icon means the paper roll is out or seated incorrectly, reload it. A red printer icon with an exclamation mark means a paper jam; open the compartment, clear any torn paper from the roller, and close the lid firmly.

Receipt prints blank or very faint: the thermal paper may be loaded with the wrong side facing up (thermal coating needs to face the print head) or the roll is old stock that has degraded, thermal paper has a shelf life of roughly 12-18 months in normal storage conditions.

Printer makes a grinding or clicking noise but doesn't feed paper: this usually indicates the roll holder spindle has come loose or the paper is jammed against the cutter bar. Power off, clear any debris, and reseat the roll before powering back on.

Error code PR-04 on screen: this is a printer head overheat protection trip, usually from printing a high volume of tickets in a short burst during peak hours. It clears itself after roughly 60 seconds of cooling and printing will resume automatically, no action needed beyond waiting.
Overview

Every new order placed through FMO arrives on the AP Smart Link terminal as an incoming order alert on [[my-orders-incoming|My Orders]], and shop staff must respond within a set time window by tapping Accept or Decline. This accept/decline step confirms to the customer that the shop has seen and is preparing their order, and is what triggers the automatic [[mkt-sms-delivery-notifications|delivery-status SMS notifications]] sent to the customer.
The incoming order screen

A new order triggers an audible alert (a repeating three-tone chime) and the screen switches to a full-screen order card showing the items, order type (delivery or collection), requested time, and a countdown timer. The default response window is 60 seconds, configurable in Settings > Orders > Response Window down to as little as 30 seconds or up to 120 seconds.

items: Green Accept button, confirms the order and sends it to print
Red Decline button, rejects the order and prompts for a reason
Amber countdown ring around the timer, turns solid red in the final 10 seconds as a visual warning

blocks.caption: Incoming order screen showing the full-screen order card with item list, countdown timer ring, and the green Accept / red Decline buttons at the bottom.

blocks.text: Declining an order

Tapping Decline brings up a short list of standard reasons: Too Busy, Item Unavailable, Closing Soon, or Other. Selecting a reason is required, it's shown to the customer and also feeds into shop performance reporting, so 'Too Busy' should only be used when genuinely at capacity rather than as a default option.
Auto-accept

Shops with consistently fast turnaround can enable Auto-Accept from Settings > Orders > Auto-Accept, which accepts every order automatically the moment it arrives, skipping the manual tap. This is not recommended for shops that regularly run out of stock on items, since there's no manual checkpoint to catch an unavailable item before it's confirmed to the customer.
What happens if no one responds

If the countdown reaches zero with no response, the order is automatically declined with reason 'No Response' and the customer is notified immediately. Repeated no-response declines are flagged on the shop's account and can affect the shop's [[mkt-customer-reviews|visibility ranking]] in the FMO app, so the terminal should always be within sight and earshot of a staff member during trading hours.
Troubleshooting

No chime or alert on new orders despite the terminal being online: check Settings > Sound > Order Alert Volume hasn't been muted, and that the terminal isn't in Do Not Disturb mode (a small crescent-moon icon in the status bar indicates this).

Order stuck on screen after tapping Accept: this usually means the print job hasn't confirmed back to the app layer. Wait 10 seconds, if the card is still frozen, tap the order number in the top corner to force-refresh the card without losing the accept status already sent.

Accept button greyed out: this happens when an item on the order has gone out of stock since it was placed. Resolve the stock conflict on screen first (mark item unavailable or override) before the Accept button becomes active again.

Orders auto-declining immediately on arrival: check that Auto-Accept and a 0-second response window aren't both misconfigured together, and confirm the terminal's clock is correct under Settings > General > Date & Time, as a clock drift can cause the countdown to expire instantly.
Overview

For delivery orders, AP Smart Link provides live driver tracking directly on the terminal, letting shop staff see where a driver is, whether they've picked up an order, and estimated arrival at the customer's address. This same tracking data powers the automatic [[mkt-sms-delivery-notifications|SMS delivery-status notifications]] sent to customers.
Assigning a driver

Once an order is [[hw-smart-link-accept-decline|accepted]] and marked ready, staff tap Assign Driver on the order card and choose from the list of drivers currently clocked in on the terminal. Drivers clock in and out using their own PIN on the terminal's Driver Login screen at the start and end of their shift, the same login used by the [[del-driver-app-overview|driver app]] on their handset.

items: Unassigned, order is ready but no driver selected yet
Assigned, driver selected, not yet marked as departed
Out for Delivery, driver has tapped Depart on their handset or the terminal
Delivered, driver or staff has marked the order complete

blocks.caption: Driver tracking screen showing a list of active drivers with status badges and a small map view with the delivery pin.

blocks.text: Live map view

Tapping a driver's name from the tracking list opens a map view showing their live position, updated roughly every 15-20 seconds while their handset has location services and mobile data active. The estimated arrival time shown is calculated from current position and typical local travel speed, and is intentionally not shown to the customer as a guaranteed time.
Multiple drivers and busy periods

During busy periods the tracking list can show up to 12 active drivers at once; beyond that it switches to a scrollable list sorted by longest-waiting order first. Staff can filter the list by status (Assigned / Out for Delivery) using the tabs along the top of the tracking screen to quickly spot orders that haven't moved.
Troubleshooting

Driver shown as 'Offline' despite being out on the road: this means their handset has lost data connection or location permissions were revoked. Ask the driver to check their phone's location toggle is on and that they have signal, the terminal will show them as active again within one location update cycle once reconnected.

Driver position frozen or stuck on an old location: this is usually a stale GPS fix rather than a lost connection. It typically self-corrects within a minute; if it persists longer than 5 minutes, have the driver toggle airplane mode on and off to force a fresh GPS lock.

Order stuck on 'Out for Delivery' long after it should have arrived: confirm with the driver directly by phone, staff can manually mark the order Delivered from the terminal if the driver confirms completion but their handset failed to update the status (a common cause is the driver's app being backgrounded by their phone's battery saver mode, see [[ts-driver-app-crash|Driver App Crashing or Freezing]] for related handset issues).

No drivers appearing in the Assign Driver list at all: check that drivers have actually clocked in via the Driver Login screen, an unclocked driver, even if physically present in shop, will not appear as assignable.
Overview

AP Smart Link needs an active internet connection, either Wi-Fi or ethernet, to receive orders in real time, process [[hw-smart-link-card-payments|card payments]], and sync [[hw-smart-link-tracking-drivers|driver tracking]]. When connectivity drops, the terminal can queue very limited activity locally but will not receive new orders until the connection is restored, this is the single most common cause of [[ts-order-not-on-terminal|a shop missing orders]], so it's worth checking regularly rather than only when a problem is reported.
Reading the status bar

items: Solid green signal icon, connected and syncing normally
Amber signal icon, connected but with high latency or intermittent packet loss
Red signal icon with a line through it, fully offline
Spinning icon next to the shop name, actively reconnecting

blocks.caption: Rear panel port layout showing the ethernet port, power input, and reset pinhole on the back of the terminal unit.

blocks.text: Wi-Fi vs ethernet

Ethernet is the more reliable option in busy kitchens where Wi-Fi signal can be disrupted by metal equipment, extraction hoods, and walk-in fridges. To switch from Wi-Fi to ethernet, simply plug in the ethernet cable to the port on the rear panel, the terminal will prefer a wired connection automatically when one is present. To configure Wi-Fi manually, go to Settings > Network > Wi-Fi, select the network, and enter the password on the on-screen keyboard.
Router and network requirements

The terminal needs outbound access on standard HTTPS (port 443) and should not be placed behind a guest network with client isolation enabled, as this blocks the terminal from reaching FMO's order servers even though it shows as 'connected' to Wi-Fi. A dedicated or unshared network connection is strongly recommended over relying on shared shop customer Wi-Fi.
Restarting the terminal

A soft restart (hold power button 10 seconds, then power back on) resolves the majority of connectivity glitches and does not affect the shop's stored menu or settings. A full network reset (Settings > Network > Reset Network Settings) clears saved Wi-Fi credentials and should only be used when changing to a new router or network name.
Troubleshooting

Terminal shows solid green connectivity but orders still aren't arriving: this is not a network fault, check Settings > Orders to confirm the shop isn't set to Paused or showing as Closed on the schedule, as this is a far more common cause than an actual dropped connection.

Wi-Fi icon repeatedly cycles between connected and disconnected: usually a weak signal at the terminal's location. Try moving the terminal closer to the router, switching to the 2.4GHz network if only 5GHz is configured (2.4GHz has better range through walls), or switching to ethernet.

Error code NET-11 shown on screen: this indicates the terminal reached the router but could not reach FMO's servers, usually a firewall or DNS issue on the shop's router. Check the router isn't blocking outbound port 443 and that DNS is set to automatic rather than a custom/restrictive DNS provider.

Terminal connects fine in the morning but drops out during lunch or dinner rush: this points to router congestion from other devices (POS systems, CCTV, customer Wi-Fi) saturating the connection at peak times. Recommend the shop put the terminal on a separate VLAN or a dedicated small router if this pattern repeats.

Reset pinhole on the rear panel does nothing when pressed: it requires a firm press with a paperclip held for a full 5 seconds, not a quick tap, this triggers a full factory reset and should only be used as a last resort under guidance from the Hardware support team, since it will require the terminal to be fully re-provisioned.
Overview

SMS campaigns let a shop send a single one-off text message to its full customer list (or a filtered segment of it) with a link straight to its FMO ordering site. Campaigns are built and sent from the Marketing dashboard, not from Smart Link, Smart Link is for order handling only. A campaign is best used for things like a new menu launch, a reopening after refurbishment, or a limited-time offer the shop wants to push in one go (see [[mkt-seasonal-campaigns|Seasonal Campaigns]] for planning these around key dates).

Every shop on a paid FMO subscription gets an SMS allowance included in their plan. Standard plans include 250 free sends per calendar month; anything beyond that is billed at 3.2p per SMS, deducted automatically from the shop's AP Funds balance. Campaign sends are metered separately from the [[mkt-sms-delivery-notifications|automatic delivery notifications]] covered in the companion article.
How to send a campaign

Staff or shop owners with marketing permissions build a campaign from Marketing > Campaigns > New SMS Campaign. The flow is the same whether it's being done by the shop themselves or by an account manager on their behalf during a support call.

items: Step 1: Choose the audience, All customers, Lapsed customers (no order in 60+ days, a good audience to pair with [[mkt-loyalty-points|Loyalty Points]] messaging), or Recent customers (ordered in last 14 days).

Step 2: Write the message. The composer enforces a 160-character limit for a single SMS segment; anything longer splits into multiple segments and multiple charges, so the character counter turns amber at 140 characters and red past 160.
Step 3: Insert the ordering link using the [SITE_LINK] token, this auto-shortens to a tracked link so open/click rates can be reported.
Step 4: Preview the message as it will appear on a customer's phone, including the sender ID (defaults to the shop's trading name, max 11 characters).
Step 5: Choose Send now or Schedule for later, scheduling supports any time up to 30 days ahead.
Step 6: Confirm, once sent, a campaign cannot be recalled or edited.

blocks.caption: Campaign composer with character counter

blocks.text: Writing an effective message
Because the character limit is tight, the message needs to lead with the offer, not a greeting. Good examples get straight to a number or a date; weak examples waste characters on filler.

items: Good: "Fri only: 20% off all orders at Spice Villa. Order now: [SITE_LINK]"
Good: "We're back! Spice Villa reopens today with 3%+ off every order. [SITE_LINK]"
Weak: "Hi there, just wanted to let you know that this week we have a great offer running, click here to see it: [SITE_LINK]" (too long, buries the offer, likely splits into 2 segments)
Weak: "Sale on now [SITE_LINK]" (no specifics, low click-through)

blocks.text: A campaign can only be sent once every 7 days per shop by default, to stop customers being over-messaged and opting out. Account managers can request a one-off exception (e.g. for a grand reopening) via a support ticket, but this is capped at two exceptions per shop per calendar year.
Common questions

"Why can't I select individual customers?", Campaigns are segment-based, not individual-recipient, to keep the tool simple and to comply with the platform's marketing consent rules. Only customers who opted into marketing communications at checkout are included in any segment.

"A customer says they never got the text", Check Marketing > Campaigns > [campaign] > Delivery Report first. Common causes are the customer having opted out, an invalid or landline number on file, or a temporary carrier delay (usually resolves within 15 minutes).

"Can we include an image or emoji?", SMS campaigns are text-only; emoji are technically allowed but count as 2 characters each toward the 160-character limit, so they're generally discouraged for shops close to the segment boundary.

"We've used our free 250 and don't want to pay for more this month", the shop can still schedule the campaign for the 1st of the next month when the allowance resets, or send to a smaller filtered segment to stay within the remaining free allowance.
Overview

Delivery status notifications are automatic, transactional SMS messages sent to a customer once their order moves to a new status in Smart Link. Unlike [[mkt-sms-sending-campaign|campaigns]], these are not opt-in marketing sends, they're treated as order-related service messages, so they go to every customer who provides a mobile number at checkout regardless of marketing consent.

There are two trigger points: 'Out for delivery' (sent when a driver marks the order as picked up on Smart Link) and 'Ready for collection' (sent when kitchen staff mark a collection order as ready). Shops running delivery-only or collection-only cannot see the notification type that doesn't apply to their order flow.
How the trigger works on Smart Link
No setup is needed for the basic notification to work, it's on by default for every shop. The trigger fires directly from the Smart Link terminal action, not from a back-office screen.

items: Delivery orders: staff tap 'Out for Delivery' on the order card in [[hw-smart-link-tracking-drivers|Smart Link]], the SMS fires within roughly 10 seconds.
Collection orders: staff tap 'Ready' on the order card, the SMS fires immediately.
If an order is later marked 'Delayed' on Smart Link, a second follow-up SMS is sent automatically with the new estimated time.
Notifications cannot be triggered manually outside of these two Smart Link actions, there is no 'resend' button for staff.

blocks.text: Message content and customisation

The message template is fixed platform-wide for consistency and cannot be edited by individual shops, this keeps the sender recognisable and avoids shops accidentally breaking the tracking link. The out-for-delivery message reads: "Your order from [Shop Name] is on its way! Estimated arrival: [ETA]." The collection message reads: "Your order from [Shop Name] is ready to collect!"

The [ETA] field pulls from the estimated delivery time the shop set when accepting the order in Smart Link, so accuracy depends on staff entering a realistic time at acceptance, not at dispatch. Shops that consistently under-estimate times see more 'where is my order' calls despite the notification being sent correctly.

blocks.caption: Smart Link order card showing the Out for Delivery action

blocks.text: Cost and volume

Delivery status notifications are included free of charge on every subscription tier and do not draw from the shop's 250-message campaign allowance, they're billed to FMO centrally as part of the platform fee, not to the shop. There is no monthly cap; a shop doing 2,000 orders a month sends 2,000+ notifications at no extra cost.
Things to check

"Customer says they got the text 20 minutes after the driver left", check the shop's Smart Link clock is synced; a common cause is staff tapping 'Out for Delivery' late rather than at actual dispatch, not a platform delay.

"Can we turn this off?", No. Because it's classed as an order-status service message rather than marketing, it cannot be disabled shop-side. If a customer wants to opt out entirely, that has to be done at the customer's account level, not the shop's.

"A customer entered their number wrong at checkout", the notification will simply fail silently; there's no error shown to the shop, and staff should tell the customer to check the order confirmation email for tracking instead.

items: No SMS sent at all: check the customer left a mobile number, not a landline (see [[customer-numbers-multiple|Customer Numbers]] for how numbers are stored against a profile).
SMS sent but ETA wrong: check the estimated time set at order acceptance, not at dispatch.
Duplicate SMS received: usually caused by staff tapping the status button twice on Smart Link.

blocks.text: Overview

Downtime promotions are scheduled discounts a shop sets up to run automatically during its quietest trading hours, the goal is to pull in orders during slow windows (a wet Tuesday afternoon, the lull between lunch and dinner) rather than discounting times that are already busy. They are configured once and then run on autopilot according to the schedule.

This is separate from the [[mkt-minimum-discount|platform-wide minimum 3% customer discount]], which applies to every order regardless of time. A downtime promotion is an additional, shop-chosen discount layered on top, active only during the windows the shop defines.
Setting up a promotion

Promotions are created from Marketing > Promotions > Downtime Promotions > New Promotion. A shop can have up to 5 active promotions running at once, each with its own schedule, similar in concept to how an [[mkt-sms-sending-campaign|SMS campaign]] is built and scheduled from the same Marketing dashboard.

items: Choose the discount type: percentage off (e.g. 10-25%) or a fixed amount off orders over a minimum spend (e.g. £3 off orders over £15).
Set the days of the week the promotion runs, any combination, including single days.
Set the start and end time for the window, minimum window length is 30 minutes, maximum is 6 hours.
Optionally cap the number of redemptions per day (useful for testing a new promotion before committing budget to it).
Name the promotion internally (customers see the discount applied at checkout, not the internal name).

blocks.text: Once saved, the promotion goes live at the next matching time window, there's no manual 'activate' step, and no need to touch Smart Link. The discount is applied automatically at checkout on the customer's ordering site when they order within the window.
Choosing good downtime windows
Account managers reviewing a shop's order-time heatmap (Reports > Order Times) can usually spot the dead zones quickly, most takeaways see a trough between 2:30pm and 5pm on weekdays.

items: Common example: 15% off, Monday-Thursday, 2:30pm-5:00pm, targets the afternoon lull.
Common example: £2 off orders over £12, Sunday-Tuesday all day, targets the quietest days of the week rather than a time window.

Common example: 20% off, weekdays 9pm-close, useful for shops that close early and want to push last-hour orders instead of wasting stock (see [[mkt-seasonal-campaigns|Seasonal Campaigns]] for planning promotions around key calendar dates too).

blocks.caption: Order-time heatmap used to choose a downtime window

blocks.text: Common questions

"Does the downtime discount stack with the 3% minimum discount?", Yes, they stack. The 3% minimum applies first as a platform rule, and the downtime promotion is applied on top during its active window.

"Can we run a promotion just for one day, like a one-off bank holiday offer?", Yes, set the schedule to only the single date's weekday and set an end date on the promotion so it doesn't recur the following week.

"We started a promotion but it's not showing at checkout", the most common cause is a timezone mismatch on the shop's Smart Link clock, or the promotion window not yet reached; promotions do not apply retroactively to orders placed just before the window opens.

"How do we know if it's working?", Marketing > Promotions > [promotion] > Performance shows redemption count, total discount given, and incremental order volume compared to the same slot in prior weeks.
Overview

Every shop on FMO applies a minimum 3% discount to every single order, every time a customer orders, not just on a first order, and not as an optional toggle. This is a platform-wide rule baked into how FMO positions itself against commission-charging competitors: customers save money on every order, permanently, as a baseline expectation of ordering through FMO.

This is one of the most common points of friction when [[sales-signing-up-new-shop|onboarding a new shop]], so it's worth understanding thoroughly before a sales or account-management conversation, since it often comes up as an objection during signup or renewal.
How the minimum discount works

The 3% figure is a floor, not a ceiling. Shops are free to set a higher standing discount if they want to compete harder on price, but they cannot go below 3% or disable it entirely. The discount is configured from Settings > Pricing > Customer Discount.

items: Default: 3% off every order, applied automatically at checkout.
Shops can raise this to any value up to 15% as a standing discount (separate from time-limited downtime promotions).
The discount applies to the food/drink subtotal, not to delivery charges or service fees.
Changes to the standing discount take effect immediately and apply to the next order placed, not retroactively.

blocks.text: Why this model is sustainable for shops

This is the question account managers get asked most: 'How can you give free marketing and a discount and still make this work for us?' The answer comes down to the commission-free structure. Shops pay a flat monthly [[sales-subscription-commission|subscription and 0% commission]] on every order, so unlike commission-based platforms, FMO isn't taking a cut of each sale. The 3% minimum discount costs the shop a small, predictable amount per order, but it's replacing what would otherwise be a 15-30% commission cut elsewhere. Even after the discount, the shop typically nets significantly more per order than on a commission-based competitor.

It's worth framing this concretely in conversation: on a £20 order, a 3% discount costs the shop 60p. On a commission platform charging 20%, the same order would cost the shop £4, over six times more.
Common questions

"Can we run the discount as a one-time new-customer offer instead?", No. The 3% minimum is deliberately not a first-order-only incentive; it's a standing feature of every order so customers build a habit of expecting savings every time, which is core to FMO's customer-acquisition pitch versus first-order-only competitor deals.

"A customer says the discount didn't apply at checkout", check Settings > Pricing > Customer Discount is still set to 3% or above; this can occasionally be misconfigured if a staff member was testing pricing changes. It should never show as 0%.

"Does the discount apply to cash orders too?", Yes, the 3% minimum applies to all orders regardless of payment method. This is distinct from the [[mkt-fmo-movement|FMO Movement]] donation option, which is card-orders-only.

"Can a shop opt out entirely if they feel margins are too tight?", No, the minimum discount is a non-negotiable condition of the FMO platform for all shops, in the same way 0% commission and the flat subscription are non-negotiable terms in the other direction.
Overview

The FMO Movement is a customer-facing initiative that lets customers donate their order discount instead of keeping it for themselves. It's opt-in and only available on card orders (it isn't offered on cash orders, since the mechanism relies on the discount being calculated and redirected at the point of card payment).

Donated discounts go toward feeding people in the customer's local community, and at scale, the aggregated donations contribute toward global hunger relief efforts, with FMO benchmarking its impact reporting against World Food Programme figures so shops and customers can see the initiative described in terms that are independently meaningful, not just an internal metric.
How it works at checkout

At the payment step on a card order, the customer sees a toggle: 'Keep my 3%+ discount' or 'Donate my discount to the FMO Movement.' It defaults to 'Keep', donation is always an active choice, never pre-selected, so shops shouldn't expect it to inflate participation automatically.

items: Only available on card payments, cash-on-delivery and cash-on-collection orders don't show the toggle.

The donated amount is exactly whatever the customer's discount would have been (the shop's [[mkt-minimum-discount|standing discount]], plus any active [[mkt-downtime-promotions|downtime promotion]]), nothing extra is taken from the shop or the customer beyond that.
Participation is tracked per shop and shown in Reports > FMO Movement > Local Impact.
There is no cost to the shop for customer participation, the shop still receives the same order total either way; only where the discount amount goes differs.

blocks.text: Using it as a marketing angle

Shops with a strong local identity, family-run takeaways, shops in tight-knit communities, often get good traction promoting their FMO Movement participation locally. It's a genuine PR angle: a shop can say 'our customers have donated £X in discounts to help feed people locally this year' without it costing the shop anything extra, since the mechanic is customer-funded, not shop-funded.

items: Suggested approach: mention participation figures in an SMS campaign (see [[mkt-sms-sending-campaign|the SMS campaign article]]) once a quarter, not every send, it loses impact if overused.
Suggested approach: print a small note on physical receipts via Smart Link referencing the shop's local impact total, refreshed monthly.
Avoid overstating it as the shop's own charitable donation, it's customer-funded and should be framed as 'our customers are doing this,' not 'we are donating.'

blocks.caption: FMO Movement toggle shown at card checkout

blocks.text: Common questions
"Can a shop see which individual customers donated?", No, participation data is aggregated for privacy; shops see totals and trends in the Local Impact report, not a customer-level breakdown.
"Can we make donation the default instead of an opt-in?", No, this is a platform-wide rule to keep the choice genuinely voluntary; it cannot be changed at shop level.

"Does participating raise our subscription cost?", No, the FMO Movement has no effect on a shop's monthly subscription or commission terms; it's entirely a customer-side choice about where their own discount goes.

"A customer asked how much of their donation actually reaches people locally", direct them to the public FMO Movement impact page rather than giving a shop-level estimate, since the local-vs-global split is calculated centrally against World Food Programme benchmarks, not per shop.
Overview

Every completed order gives the customer the option to leave a star rating and written review of the shop. Reviews are one of the single biggest factors in whether a new customer chooses a shop over a nearby competitor when browsing FMO, more influential in early testing than price alone in many categories.

Reviews are permanent once submitted: shops cannot delete or edit a review left about them, including negative ones. This is a deliberate platform rule to keep reviews trustworthy for other customers, and it's important staff set this expectation clearly with shop owners during [[sales-signing-up-new-shop|onboarding]] so it isn't a surprise later.
How reviews affect visibility

A shop's average rating and review count feed directly into its ranking position in FMO's local search and browse results. Two shops at similar distance and price point can see meaningfully different order volume purely based on review strength.

items: Shops need a minimum of 5 reviews before an average star rating displays publicly, below that, the listing shows 'New' instead of a star score.
Ranking weighting favours recency as well as volume, a shop with 40 reviews all from over a year ago ranks lower on this factor than one with 15 reviews from the last month.
A single 1-star review has limited impact once a shop has 20+ reviews, but can noticeably drag down a newer shop's average.

blocks.text: Encouraging more reviews

Shops can't pay for reviews, filter which ones show, or offer discounts explicitly in exchange for a review (this breaches platform terms and is treated as review manipulation if reported). What they can do is make it easy and natural for satisfied customers to leave one.

items: Encourage staff to mention, verbally at handover or on the phone, that feedback helps the shop, a light verbal nudge, not a scripted request tied to a reward.

Use the [[mkt-sms-delivery-notifications|delivery/collection notification]] window as a natural moment, customers are most likely to review within about 2 hours of their order being marked delivered or collected, while the experience is fresh.

Respond to reviews (shops can reply publicly to any review, positive or negative, even though they can't edit or remove them), a considered reply to a negative review is often visible to far more prospective customers than the original complaint.

blocks.caption: Shop listing showing star rating and recent reviews

blocks.text: Common questions

"A customer left a review about the wrong shop", this does happen occasionally with similarly named shops; it should be reported via Support > Report an Issue with the order ID so it can be investigated and moved or removed centrally, shops themselves have no removal tool.

"A review mentions something factually false, like a wrong allergy claim", the shop can post a public reply correcting the record; outright false or defamatory content can be escalated to support for review, but a merely negative or harsh review that's the customer's genuine opinion will not be removed.

"Can a shop offer a discount code in exchange for a good review?", No, incentivising reviews in exchange for a rating (positive or otherwise) is against platform terms; it can result in reviews being flagged and, for repeated breaches, a shop's review display being suspended (see [[acc-account-suspension|Account Suspension]] for the wider causes and reinstatement process).

"How long before a new review appears publicly?", Reviews are published near-instantly, though very new shops may see a short manual moderation delay (typically under 24 hours) while the review content is automatically screened for prohibited content.
Overview

AP Funds is FMO's real-time balance system for online card takings. Instead of a shop waiting for card payments to clear through the banking network, every online order paid by card is reflected in the shop's AP Funds balance the moment the order is confirmed on Smart Link. This gives shop owners a live, accurate view of cash they've actually earned that day, rather than an estimate based on projected sales.

AP Funds sits between the customer's payment and the shop's own bank account. It is not a loan or a credit facility - it is simply the shop's own money, made visible and usable before the underlying bank settlement completes.
How it works

items: A customer pays online by card through the FMO ordering site or app.
The order is accepted on the shop's Smart Link terminal and the payment is authorised.
The AP Funds balance updates within seconds - visible to the shop owner in the FMO Partner App under Balance > AP Funds.

The shop can then choose to [[sales-getting-paid-timelines|withdraw to their bank account]], request a [[request-funds-same-day|same-day transfer]], or spend directly via the [[sales-advantage-card|Advantage Card]] (once issued).

blocks.text: AP Funds balances only include online card payments processed through FMO. Cash orders, and card payments taken on a shop's own separate card machine outside of FMO, are not reflected in the AP Funds balance.

blocks.caption: FMO Partner App showing the AP Funds balance updating in real time as an order is paid for

blocks.text: Eligibility and requirements

items: Shop must have completed [[acc-kyc-verification|identity and business verification]] (Companies House or sole trader ID check).
Smart Link terminal must be [[hw-smart-link-connectivity|active and reporting]] - a terminal offline for more than 48 hours will pause AP Funds updates until reconnected.
A verified UK business bank account must be linked under Accounts > Payout Settings before funds can be withdrawn (the balance itself will still accrue without this).

blocks.text: New shops typically see AP Funds active from their first live online order - there is no separate sign-up process, as it is built into every FMO account by default at no extra cost.
Common questions

A shop reports their AP Funds balance hasn't moved despite taking orders all day. First check whether Smart Link is showing as online in Accounts > Devices - a terminal that has lost connection will still take orders locally but won't sync balance updates until it reconnects.

A shop asks whether AP Funds includes their card machine takings for walk-in customers. It does not - AP Funds only reflects online orders placed and paid through FMO's platform, not any in-store card terminal the shop uses independently.

A shop wants to know if there's a cap on how much can sit in the AP Funds balance. There isn't a hard cap, but balances over £5,000 held for more than 10 days may trigger an automatic review prompt in Accounts, as a routine fraud-prevention check - this is normal and doesn't affect the shop's ability to use the funds.
Overview

Once a shop chooses to move money out of their [[sales-ap-funds|AP Funds]] balance into their linked bank account (see [[sales-updating-shop-details|Account Details]] for how to change which account payouts land in), FMO offers two payout speeds: the standard free transfer, and a paid same-day transfer for shops that need funds sooner. Both are initiated from the same place in the Partner App or CRM.
Standard bank transfer

The standard transfer takes 3-5 business days to land in the shop's bank account, counted from the day the transfer is requested. Weekends and UK bank holidays do not count towards this window, so a transfer requested on a Friday will typically not begin counting its business days until the following Monday.

items: No fee for standard transfers - included in every FMO [[sales-subscription-commission|subscription]].
Requests submitted before 11:59pm are queued for processing the next business day.
Funds are sent via Faster Payments where the receiving bank supports it, otherwise BACS.

blocks.text: Same-day transfer

Shops that need faster access can request a same-day transfer for a flat fee of £4.99 per transfer. This is available from Accounts > Payout Settings > Request Transfer, with 'Same-day' selectable as an option alongside 'Standard'.

items: Cut-off time is 2:00pm on any business day - requests made after this are automatically processed as next-business-day standard transfers instead.
Same-day transfers use Faster Payments only, so the receiving bank must support it (the large majority of UK banks do).
The £4.99 fee is deducted from the transferred amount, not charged separately to the shop's card or subscription.

blocks.caption: Payout settings screen showing transfer options, cut-off time, and the same-day transfer fee

blocks.text: Things to check

A shop calls saying their standard transfer is on day 6 and still hasn't arrived. Confirm the request date and count only business days, excluding any bank holiday in the window - for example, a transfer requested the Wednesday before a bank holiday Monday will show as later than shops expect. If it's genuinely beyond 5 business days, escalate to Accounts with the transfer reference.

A shop asks if they can get a same-day transfer for an amount just submitted at 2:15pm. They can't - it will have already been queued as standard once the 2:00pm cut-off passed, and there's no way to manually override this in the CRM.

A shop wants to switch every payout to same-day going forward rather than requesting it manually each time. There's no 'always same-day' setting currently - each transfer is requested individually, so this is worth setting expectations on if a shop asks for automatic same-day payouts.
Overview

FMO's pricing model is built around two simple components: a flat monthly subscription and 0% commission on every order. This is a deliberate point of difference from marketplace-style platforms that take a percentage cut of each sale, and it's one of the strongest selling points when onboarding a new shop.
The subscription
