Shops pay one flat monthly fee regardless of how many orders they take. The fee covers use of the Smart Link terminal, online ordering website and app listing, AP Funds, and standard customer support. There is no per-order charge layered on top.

items: Subscription is billed monthly in advance, taken automatically from the shop's linked payment method.
Standard subscription tier: £39.99/month for a single-site shop.
[[sales-multi-site-accounts|Multi-site or group accounts]] are quoted individually by the Accounts team based on number of locations.

blocks.text: 0% commission

Every order placed through FMO's online ordering channel carries 0% commission - the shop keeps 100% of the order value (minus the [[mkt-minimum-discount|standard minimum 3% customer discount]] applied at checkout, which comes off the customer's total, not the shop's takings). This applies uniformly whether the order is collection or delivery, and regardless of order size.

The minimum 3% customer discount is separate from commission - it's a saving passed to the customer to encourage them to order directly rather than through third-party marketplace apps, and it is factored into the shop's pricing setup during onboarding.
No hidden charges

items: No per-order commission or transaction percentage.
No listing fee, no setup fee for standard single-site onboarding.
No charge for standard 3-5 day bank transfers.
The only optional extra cost is the [[sales-getting-paid-timelines|£4.99 same-day transfer fee]], charged only when a shop chooses to use it.

blocks.caption: Billing summary screen showing the flat monthly subscription with 0% commission on all orders

blocks.text: Common questions

A prospective shop owner asks how FMO makes money if there's no commission. Explain that revenue comes solely from the flat subscription - this is precisely why FMO doesn't need to take a cut of each order, unlike commission-based marketplace competitors.

An existing shop asks why a card payment processing charge appears on their [[sales-vat-invoicing|statement]]. Card processing fees for online payments are a separate pass-through cost from the payment provider (typically around 1.4% + 20p per transaction) and are not part of FMO's subscription or commission - this should be clearly distinguished from commission when explaining a statement.

A shop wants to know if the subscription price can be reduced if they take low order volumes. The subscription is flat regardless of volume - there's no tiered pricing based on order count for single-site shops, though this can be flagged to Accounts for review in exceptional cases.
Overview

Onboarding a new shop onto FMO is a sales-led process that typically takes a few working days from a signed agreement to the shop going live and taking its first online order. This article covers the steps sales staff should follow and what to expect at each stage.
Step 1: Initial visit and business details

The sales rep collects core business details during the initial visit or call: legal business name, trading name, business address, contact details, and business type (sole trader, partnership, or limited company). These are entered into the CRM under Leads > New Shop > Business Details.

items: Business registration number (Companies House number if limited company).
VAT number if applicable.
Primary contact name, mobile number, and email.
Cuisine type and expected weekly order volume (used for onboarding team prioritisation).

blocks.text: Step 2: Signed agreement

The shop owner signs the FMO partner agreement, either digitally via the CRM's e-sign link or on paper during the visit. The agreement confirms the subscription tier, sets out the 0% commission and minimum 3% customer discount terms, and authorises FMO to ship a Smart Link terminal to the registered business address.
Step 3: Terminal shipping and menu setup

items: [[hw-smart-link-getting-started|Smart Link terminal]] is shipped pre-configured to the shop's account - typically arrives within 2-3 working days via tracked courier.

[[menu-availability|Menu setup]] can be completed by the shop owner themselves via the Partner App, or handed to FMO's onboarding team by selecting 'Assisted Menu Setup' in the CRM (usually completed within 1 working day of receiving menu details).
Photos, pricing, item descriptions, and allergen information should be finalised before going live.

blocks.caption: Onboarding checklist in the CRM showing agreement signed, terminal shipped, and menu setup status

blocks.text: Step 4: Verification and going live

Before the shop can accept live orders, Accounts completes [[acc-kyc-verification|identity]] and bank verification (see [[sales-advantage-card|Advantage Card]] and [[sales-updating-shop-details|account update]] articles for document requirements). Once verification clears and Smart Link is confirmed online, the shop's listing is switched to active and customers can begin ordering.

Typical end-to-end timeline is 3-5 working days from signed agreement to going live, assuming menu content and verification documents are provided promptly. Delays are most commonly caused by missing bank verification documents or incomplete menu content.
Common questions

A sales rep asks whether a shop can go live before their Smart Link terminal arrives. They can't - Smart Link is required to receive and confirm orders, so the shop must wait for the terminal and confirm it's online before the listing is activated.

A shop owner asks if they can do their own menu setup instead of waiting for the onboarding team. Yes - this is often faster, and can be done any time after the agreement is signed via the Partner App, without waiting on FMO staff.

A rep asks what happens if a shop fails identity verification. The account remains in a pending state and cannot go live; Accounts will contact the shop directly to request corrected or additional documents, and sales should not treat the deal as closed until verification clears.
Overview

The Advantage Card is a physical card that lets a verified shop owner draw directly on their AP Funds balance, similar to using a debit card. It's designed to give shop owners immediate, everyday access to money they've already earned through online orders, without needing to wait for a bank transfer first.
How it ties into AP Funds

The Advantage Card draws its balance directly from [[sales-ap-funds|AP Funds]] - as online card orders come in and the AP Funds balance updates in real time, that same balance is what's available to spend on the Advantage Card. There's no need to [[sales-getting-paid-timelines|move money to a bank account]] first; the card simply spends against the live AP Funds balance.

items: Works anywhere Mastercard is accepted, in-store and online.
Contactless and chip-and-PIN enabled.
Balance and recent transactions visible in the Partner App under Balance > Advantage Card.

blocks.text: Eligibility

The Advantage Card is issued automatically once a shop's account passes [[acc-kyc-verification|full verification]] - it isn't something that has to be separately requested by most shops. Verification requires:

items: Proof of identity for the account holder (passport or UK driving licence).
Proof of business address (recent utility bill or business bank statement, dated within 3 months).
Confirmation of the linked bank account under Accounts > Payout Settings.
For limited companies, confirmation of the registered director matches the account holder on file.

blocks.text: Once documents are submitted, verification typically takes 2-4 working days. The Advantage Card is then shipped to the registered business address, arriving within 5-7 working days.

blocks.caption: Partner App view of the Advantage Card balance and recent transaction history

blocks.text: Limits and fees

items: Daily spend limit of £1,500 by default (can be increased on request, subject to Accounts review).
No fee for card issue or standard use within the UK.
ATM withdrawals carry a £1.50 flat fee per withdrawal.
Overseas transactions carry a 2.5% foreign transaction fee.

blocks.text: Common questions

A shop owner says their Advantage Card was declined despite having a healthy AP Funds balance. Check whether the daily spend limit of £1,500 has been reached - this resets at midnight, and a temporary limit increase can be requested through Accounts if the shop has a recurring need for larger single transactions.

A shop asks why they haven't received an Advantage Card despite being live on FMO for weeks. This usually means verification hasn't been completed - check Accounts > Verification Status, as an incomplete document set (commonly a missing proof of address) will hold the card from being issued indefinitely until resolved.

A shop owner reports their Advantage Card was lost or stolen. This should be treated urgently - the card can be frozen instantly from the Partner App under Balance > Advantage Card > Freeze Card, and a replacement can be ordered from the same screen, arriving within 5-7 working days.
Overview

Shop owners can self-service most of their account information directly through the Partner App, without needing to contact FMO staff. Some changes, however - particularly around banking and ownership - require verification or must be routed through Sales & Accounts for security reasons.
What shops can update themselves
The following can be changed instantly by the shop owner via Account > Shop Details in the Partner App, with no approval needed:

items: Business address and shop opening hours.
Contact phone number and email address.
Menu items, pricing, and photos.
Notification preferences and [[mkt-sms-sending-campaign|marketing opt-ins]].

blocks.text: Changes to opening hours or address take effect immediately on the public-facing ordering site. Changes to contact details take effect immediately in the CRM but may take up to 15 minutes to sync to SMS/email notification systems.
Changes that require verification
Bank account changes are the most common verification-gated change. A shop requesting to change the bank account linked for payouts must submit:

items: A recent bank statement or void cheque confirming the new account details.
Confirmation the new account is held in the same business name as the FMO account (or a satisfactory explanation if not).
Re-confirmation of identity if the request comes more than 12 months after the last verification check.

blocks.text: Bank account changes are submitted via Accounts > Payout Settings > Request Change, and reviewed by the Accounts team - typical turnaround is 1-2 working days. During this review window, any [[sales-getting-paid-timelines|pending payouts]] are held rather than sent to the old account.

blocks.caption: Account details screen showing self-service fields versus fields flagged as requiring verification

blocks.text: Ownership changes

Ownership changes - a new owner taking over an existing shop, or a change in the registered director for a limited company - always go through Sales & Accounts and cannot be self-served. This requires a new verification pass under the incoming owner's name, a new signed agreement, and confirmation of how the AP Funds balance and any outstanding payouts are to be handled at handover.
Things to check

A shop calls asking to update their bank account because their old business account was closed. Treat this as a standard bank change request - collect a new bank statement and confirm the business name matches, then submit via Accounts > Payout Settings > Request Change; don't attempt to edit this directly as it isn't a self-service field.

A shop is being sold and the buyer wants to keep the same Smart Link terminal and menu setup. This is an ownership change, not a simple details update - route it to [[sales-signing-up-new-shop|Sales & Accounts]] so the incoming owner can be [[acc-kyc-verification|verified]] separately and a new agreement signed before AP Funds and payouts are transferred to their name.

A shop owner says their updated phone number isn't receiving order notification texts yet. Check whether the change was made within the last 15 minutes, as sync to the notification system isn't instant; if it's been longer than that, escalate as a technical fault rather than treating it as expected delay.
Overview

A customer contacts support saying they placed an order and paid, but the shop is telling them nothing has come through on Smart Link. This is one of the more time-sensitive tickets we handle, because food is time-critical and the customer is usually waiting at home wondering whether to order elsewhere. Before assuming a hardware fault, work through the checklist below in order, most cases resolve at step 1 or 2.
Step-by-step diagnosis

items: Confirm in the Order Management screen (Orders > Order Lookup) that the order has a status of 'Sent to Terminal' or later, if it's stuck at 'Payment Authorised', the order never left our system and this is not a terminal issue.

Check the shop's [[hw-smart-link-connectivity|Smart Link connectivity]] indicator on the Shop Status dashboard, a solid green dot means online, amber means intermittent signal, red means offline for more than 5 minutes.

Ask the shop staff to check the terminal's order queue tab directly, not just the printed receipt tray, orders can arrive silently if the [[hw-smart-link-printing-receipts|printer has jammed]] or run out of paper.

Check whether the shop has a second device (some multi-site shops run Smart Link on a tablet and a countertop unit), orders occasionally route to the wrong paired device after a [[hw-smart-link-firmware-updates|firmware update]].
Ask the customer to confirm the shop name and branch shown on their confirmation email matches the shop they're calling, duplicate shop names in the same postcode are a common source of confusion.

blocks.caption: Terminal connectivity indicator on the Shop Status dashboard

blocks.text: Common error messages and what they mean

items: 'ERR-204 Sync Timeout' on the terminal screen, Smart Link lost connection to FMO's order relay mid-transfer; the order is queued and will retry automatically for up to 10 minutes.

'No signal' banner across the top of the terminal, local Wi-Fi or ethernet has dropped; this is a shop-side network issue, not an FMO outage, unless Shop Status also shows red for multiple shops in the area.

Order shows in Order Lookup as 'Delivered to Terminal' but the shop denies receiving it, most often a paper jam or the shop's audible alert being muted; ask them to check Settings > Notifications on the unit.

blocks.text: What to tell the customer

Reassure the customer that their payment is safe and that we are actively checking with the shop. Avoid promising a specific resolution time until you've confirmed the terminal status, since a red connectivity indicator can mean anywhere from 2 minutes to over an hour depending on the cause. If the order has genuinely not reached the shop and is unlikely to in a reasonable time, offer to cancel the unaccepted order so the customer can order elsewhere, see the '[[ts-cancelling-accepted-order|Cancelling an Order After Acceptance]]' article for the cancellation boundary.
Escalation

If the Shop Status dashboard shows the terminal red for more than 15 minutes with no self-recovery, escalate to the Hardware team via the Support queue, tagging the ticket 'Smart Link-Offline' and including the shop ID and the order reference.

items: If more than one shop in the same postcode area is showing red simultaneously, escalate immediately to Hardware as a possible regional relay outage rather than an individual unit fault.

If Order Lookup shows the order stuck at 'Sent to Terminal' for over 20 minutes with no shop-side explanation, escalate to the Platform team, this points to a relay-side delivery failure rather than a shop connectivity issue.
Do not close the ticket until the order shows either 'Accepted' or 'Cancelled' in Order Lookup, even if the customer says they've resolved it by phone with the shop directly.

blocks.text: Overview

Customers sometimes report that although their order went through and payment was taken, they never received a confirmation email. In the large majority of cases the order itself is fine and this is purely an email delivery issue. Treat this as a low-urgency ticket unless the customer also can't see the order status, in which case follow the diagnosis steps here first before escalating.
Step-by-step diagnosis

items: Confirm the order exists and has a valid status in Order Lookup (the same screen used in [[ts-order-not-on-terminal|Order Not Appearing on Smart Link]]), if it does, the order is fine regardless of the email issue, and you can reassure the customer on that point immediately.
Ask the customer to check their Junk, Spam, and Promotions folders, this resolves roughly two-thirds of these tickets.

Verify the email address on the order in Order Lookup character-by-character against what the customer gives you, common issues are missing dots, transposed letters, or an old address saved from a previous order.

Check the Email Delivery Log (Tools > Email Log, searchable by order reference) for a 'Bounced' or 'Deferred' status, a bounce usually confirms a bad address, while 'Deferred' means the receiving mail server is temporarily rejecting our messages.
Ask if the customer uses a corporate or school email address, some corporate spam filters block automated order confirmation senders outright.

blocks.text: Reading the Email Delivery Log

items: 'Delivered', the email left our system and was accepted by the customer's mail server; if they still can't find it, it's very likely in Spam or was filtered silently.
'Bounced - Hard Fail', the address doesn't exist or is misspelled; the order should be corrected on file, but note this doesn't affect the order itself, only future emails.
'Bounced - Mailbox Full', customer's inbox is over quota; nothing FMO can do, advise the customer to clear space or use another address next time.
'Deferred x3', the receiving server queued and is retrying; can take up to 24 hours to finally deliver or bounce.

blocks.text: What to tell the customer

Confirm their order is confirmed and active regardless of the missing email, the email is a convenience, not proof of the order. Offer to read out or resend the order summary verbally or via [[mkt-sms-delivery-notifications|SMS]] if available on their account. If the email address on file is wrong, offer to correct it for future orders, but note that reissuing a confirmation to a corrected address for THIS order is not currently possible, only a manual summary can be provided.
Escalation
Most cases resolve without escalation once the customer checks spam or you confirm the order status verbally. Escalate only in the narrower cases below.

items: If the Email Delivery Log shows 'Delivered' but the customer insists after checking spam it is nowhere to be found, and this affects multiple recent orders, escalate to the Email Systems team with the order reference and delivery log timestamp, this can indicate a filtering rule on our sending domain.
If more than a handful of similar tickets appear within the same hour, escalate to Email Systems immediately as a possible send-side outage rather than logging each individually.
Do not escalate simple bounced/misspelled address cases, correct the record and close the ticket.

blocks.text: Overview

A shop can decline an order after payment has been authorised, for example if they're too busy, out of an ingredient, or closing early. When this happens, customers frequently see the transaction still sitting on their bank statement or banking app as 'pending' and worry they've been charged for food they're not getting. This article explains what's actually happening and how to talk the customer through it.
What actually happens when an order is declined

When a shop [[hw-smart-link-accept-decline|declines an order]], FMO does not take the customer's money. What the customer sees on their bank statement is an authorisation hold, not a completed payment, it's the bank reserving the funds at the moment of checkout, before the shop has even accepted. When the shop declines, FMO releases the hold on our end immediately, but the customer's bank still needs to process that release internally before the funds show as available again.

items: Debit card holds: typically release within 3-5 working days, though some banks clear same-day.
Credit card holds: can take up to 7 working days depending on the issuer.
The exact release timing is controlled entirely by the customer's bank, not by FMO or the shop, this is standard card network behaviour, not something specific to our platform.

blocks.text: Step-by-step diagnosis

items: Look up the order in Order Lookup and confirm the status reads 'Declined by Shop' with a timestamp.
Check the Decline Reason field, shops are prompted to select a reason (e.g. 'Kitchen closed', '[[menu-availability|Item unavailable]]', 'Too busy') and this is often useful context for the customer.

Confirm in the Payments tab that the transaction shows 'Authorisation Released' on our side, if it still shows 'Authorised' and hasn't released after more than 30 minutes, this needs escalation rather than a standard explanation.
Ask the customer which bank or card provider they use, since release timelines genuinely vary, this helps set accurate expectations rather than a generic answer.

blocks.caption: Order status flowchart: Authorised, Declined, Released

blocks.text: What to tell the customer

items: "The shop wasn't able to take your order this time, and importantly, no money has actually been taken from you."
"What you're seeing is a temporary hold your bank places when an order is placed, this is standard practice across all [[hw-smart-link-card-payments|card payments]], not just ours."
"We've already released the hold on our side. Your bank should clear it automatically within 3 to 7 working days, we're not able to speed this up as it's entirely a banking process."
"If it's still showing after 7 working days, please contact your bank directly and reference the authorisation date, they'll be able to look into it faster than we can from our end."

blocks.text: Escalation
Escalation is rarely needed for the hold timeline itself, since that is outside our control. It is needed when our own system has not correctly released the authorisation.

items: If the Payments tab shows the authorisation still 'Authorised' (not 'Released') more than 30 minutes after the shop declined, escalate to the Payments team via the Support queue with the transaction ID, this indicates a release failure on our side, not a bank delay.

If the customer reports the hold has not cleared after 10 working days, escalate to Payments to confirm our release was sent correctly, so they can provide the customer with documentation for their bank if needed.
Never tell a customer FMO can force an early release of funds, this is not possible and setting that expectation causes repeat contacts.

blocks.text: Overview

A customer enters their postcode on the FMO site or app and sees no shops listed, or very few compared to what they expect. This is almost always a coverage gap, not a fault, FMO's shop network grows continuously as new takeaways [[sales-signing-up-new-shop|sign up]], and coverage (see [[del-delivery-zones|Delivery Zones]] for how a shop's own coverage area is defined once live) is uneven across the country at any given time. This article explains how to check and explain this clearly.
Step-by-step diagnosis

items: Search the exact postcode in the Coverage Lookup tool (Tools > Coverage Lookup) to confirm zero or low results, don't rely on the customer's description alone, as postcode entry errors are common.

Try the outward code only (e.g. 'SW1A' instead of 'SW1A 1AA') to see if nearby areas within the same postal district have any shops, this tells you whether it's a hyperlocal gap or a wider regional one.

Check the Sales Pipeline dashboard for that region to see if any shops are currently in [[sales-signing-up-new-shop|onboarding]], if so, you can give the customer a general sense that coverage is expanding without promising a date.
Confirm the customer isn't using an old cached version of the app or site, occasionally a shop has signed up but a customer's app hasn't refreshed its local coverage cache.

blocks.text: Why this happens

FMO doesn't blanket-cover the country in one go, coverage is built shop by shop as independent takeaways sign up to the platform. A postcode showing no results simply means no shop in that immediate area has joined FMO yet, not that there's a technical fault or that FMO has excluded the area deliberately. Rural areas and smaller towns naturally lag behind cities, and this changes on an ongoing basis as new sign-ups come through the Sales team.
What to tell the customer

items: "It looks like we don't have any shops signed up in your immediate area just yet, that's not a fault on your end, it simply means no takeaway there has joined FMO so far."
"We're adding new shops all the time, so this can change, I'd recommend checking back every few weeks."
"If there's a specific takeaway you'd like to see on FMO, I can log that as a shop referral for our Sales team to reach out to them."
Avoid giving a specific date or promise for when coverage will arrive, onboarding timelines are outside support's visibility and vary shop to shop.

blocks.text: Logging a shop referral

If the customer names a specific local takeaway they'd like to see on the platform, log it via Tools > Shop Referral with the shop name, approximate location, and customer postcode. This feeds directly into the Sales team's regional prospecting list and is the single most useful action you can take on this ticket type.
Escalation
This ticket type rarely needs technical escalation since it reflects real coverage, not a bug. Escalate only in these specific situations.

items: If Coverage Lookup shows shops ARE listed for the postcode but the customer-facing app or site shows none, escalate to the Platform team as a possible display or caching bug, including the postcode and a screenshot if the customer can provide one.

If several customers from the same postal district report the same discrepancy within a short window, escalate immediately rather than logging individually, this suggests a regional sync issue rather than isolated coverage gaps.
For general 'when will my area get coverage' pressure from a customer, redirect to the Shop Referral process rather than escalating, Sales, not Support, owns onboarding timelines.

blocks.text: Overview

Customers sometimes discover an error on an order after it has been placed, wrong item, wrong size, wrong address, or a missing special request such as an allergy note. What support can and can't do depends entirely on the order's acceptance status, so establishing that first is the most important step in every ticket of this type.
Step-by-step diagnosis

items: Look up the order in Order Lookup and check the status field first, this determines everything that follows.

If status is 'Pending Acceptance' or 'Sent to Terminal' (not yet accepted): the order can still be amended or cancelled by the customer, so guide them to the app's Order Details screen and the 'Edit Order' or 'Cancel Order' button.

If status is 'Accepted': the shop has taken responsibility for fulfilling the order and food preparation may already be underway, FMO cannot use [[edit-order-updating|Edit Order]] on the shop's system from our side.
Identify the type of mistake, since the right next step differs: item/quantity error, delivery address error, allergy/dietary note omission, or payment/discount code error.

blocks.text: Handling by mistake type (accepted orders)

items: Wrong item or quantity: advise the customer to contact the shop directly using the shop's phone number shown on their order confirmation, the shop can often correct this before the order leaves the kitchen if caught quickly.

Wrong delivery address: this is urgent, advise the customer to call the shop immediately, as delivery drivers are usually dispatched with the address already loaded and this is the one error type where minutes matter.

Missing [[acc-allergen-info|allergy or dietary]] note: treat as urgent regardless of prep stage, advise the customer to call the shop straight away so kitchen staff can be alerted before the food is packaged.

Incorrect discount or payment amount: this is the one category support can review directly, check the Payments tab for the applied [[mkt-downtime-promotions|discount code]] and escalate to Payments if the wrong amount was charged, since this isn't something the shop controls.

blocks.caption: Order status flowchart: Pending, Accepted, Fulfilled

blocks.text: What to tell the customer

items: "I can see the shop has already accepted your order, which means they've taken it on and may have started preparing it, because of that, we're not able to change the order details from our side."
"Your best and fastest option is to call the shop directly on the number in your confirmation email or SMS, they can amend it in the kitchen if you reach them in time."
"If it's an allergy concern, please stress that clearly when you call, shops treat allergy corrections as a priority."
"If the item you received doesn't match what you ordered and the shop can't resolve it, let us know afterwards and we can look at that separately."

blocks.text: Escalation

Because shops own fulfilment once an order is accepted, most 'mistake on order' tickets are resolved by directing the customer to the shop rather than by FMO escalation. Escalate in the following specific cases only.

items: If the customer says they called the shop repeatedly with no answer during business hours, escalate to the Shop Relations team with the shop ID and times called, as this may indicate a wider responsiveness issue with that shop.
If the mistake involves an incorrect charge or discount code, escalate to Payments with the order reference and the discount code used, do not attempt to manually adjust charges yourself.

If an allergy complaint results in a medical reaction being reported, escalate immediately to the Food Safety & Compliance team via the priority queue, regardless of order status or time of day, this overrides the standard 'contact the shop' guidance.

blocks.text: Overview

One of the most common support requests is a customer asking to cancel an order they've changed their mind about, or ordered by mistake, after the shop has already accepted it. This article explains the acceptance boundary clearly and gives the exact wording to use, since this is a frequent source of frustration if not explained well.
The acceptance boundary

An order can be freely cancelled by the customer at any point before the shop accepts it, this covers the window from checkout through to 'Pending Acceptance' and 'Sent to Terminal' status. Once a shop [[hw-smart-link-accept-decline|presses Accept]] on Smart Link, responsibility for that order transfers to the shop, and food preparation may begin immediately. From that point, FMO cannot cancel the order on the customer's behalf, because we have no way of knowing or controlling what stage of preparation the kitchen is at.
Step-by-step diagnosis

items: Look up the order in Order Lookup and check the status field.

'Pending Acceptance' or 'Sent to Terminal': cancellation is straightforward, guide the customer to the 'Cancel Order' button in their Order Details screen, or cancel it directly from Order Lookup using the Cancel action if the customer is unable to.
'Accepted': cancellation is no longer available through FMO; the customer must contact the shop directly.
'Out for Delivery' or 'Ready for Collection': cancellation is essentially never appropriate at this stage, advise the customer accordingly and manage expectations firmly but politely.

Check the timestamp of acceptance versus now, if acceptance happened less than 60 seconds ago, it's occasionally worth suggesting the customer try calling immediately, as very early-stage prep may still be able to stop, though this is entirely the shop's discretion, not a guarantee.

blocks.text: What to tell the customer

items: "I can see the shop has already accepted your order, which means they've started working on it, so unfortunately we're not able to cancel it from our end."
"Your best option is to call the shop directly on the number shown in your order confirmation, they're the only ones able to stop preparation at this stage."

"I know that's frustrating, especially if this happened quickly, but once a shop accepts, they take full responsibility for that order, and cancelling from our side isn't something we're able to override."
"If the shop agrees to cancel on their end, they'll process it and any refund from there, we're not able to do that centrally once it's accepted."

blocks.text: Handling pushback

Customers sometimes push back, pointing out that they cancelled 'seconds' after ordering or that the shop hasn't actually started cooking yet. Stay firm but empathetic: explain that FMO has no visibility into kitchen prep status, only the acceptance event itself, so we can't make judgment calls about whether cancellation is 'safe' at that point, only the shop can. Do not cancel an accepted order manually in Order Lookup under any circumstances, even under customer pressure, as this bypasses the shop's ownership of the order and can cause payment and stock discrepancies for the shop.
Escalation
Most tickets of this type close once the customer understands the acceptance boundary and is redirected to the shop. Escalate only in the cases below.

items: If the customer reports the shop refused to cancel or was unhelpful about an order that is clearly a duplicate or accidental double-order, escalate to Shop Relations with both order references so they can review the shop's conduct.

If a customer disputes a charge because a shop cancelled very late and they believe they were charged in error, escalate to Payments rather than attempting to resolve the [[ts-payment-taken-order-declined|charge dispute]] yourself.

Never override the acceptance boundary manually, even for a distressed or repeat-contact customer, if a genuine exception seems warranted (e.g. [[acc-account-suspension|suspected fraud on the account]]), escalate to the Support Team Lead for a judgment call rather than acting unilaterally.

blocks.text: Overview

The Driver App is the companion handset app that delivery drivers use alongside a shop's AP Smart Link terminal. It handles clock-in/clock-out, receiving delivery assignments, in-app navigation, and reporting delivery status back to the shop in real time. It is the piece that makes [[hw-smart-link-tracking-drivers|the driver tracking screen on Smart Link]] actually work, without it running correctly on a driver's phone, the terminal has nothing to show.

The app is free for drivers to install and is tied to the shop's account rather than to an individual driver profile that follows them between shops, a driver working shifts at two different FMO shops needs to be added and clocked in separately at each one under Settings > Drivers > Manage Drivers on the terminal.
Clocking in and out

A driver clocks in either from their own handset via the Driver App's Clock In button, or directly on the terminal's Driver Login screen using their 4-digit PIN, set for them by the shop under Settings > Drivers > Manage Drivers. Clocking in on either device syncs to both within a few seconds. Once clocked in, the driver becomes selectable in the Assign Driver list covered in the driver tracking article, and their pay clock for the shift starts, see [[del-driver-pay|how driver pay is calculated]] for how clocked hours feed into earnings.

items: Drivers must have location services and mobile data enabled before clocking in, the app blocks clock-in with 'Location Required' if either is off.
A driver can only be clocked in at one shop at a time, attempting to clock in elsewhere while already active shows 'Already Clocked In at [Shop Name]'.
Clocking out is blocked while a driver has an order marked Out for Delivery against them, they must mark it Delivered first.
Shifts longer than 12 hours trigger an automatic prompt asking the driver to confirm they're still working, to catch a forgotten clock-out.

blocks.text: Receiving and handling a delivery

When shop staff tap Assign Driver on an order, the assigned driver gets a push notification on the Driver App showing the customer's address, order reference, and any driver notes left by staff. The driver taps Accept Job (this is separate from the shop-side order acceptance covered in the accepting orders article, it just confirms the driver has seen the assignment) and then Depart once they've left the shop with the order, which is what flips the order to Out for Delivery on the terminal.

blocks.caption: Driver App home screen showing an active delivery card with the customer address, a Depart button, and the day's clocked-in hours in the top bar.

blocks.text: The app's built-in navigation opens the destination in the driver's preferred maps app (Google Maps or Apple Maps, set under the app's own Settings > Navigation) rather than routing inside the Driver App itself, since building dedicated turn-by-turn navigation isn't necessary when the phone's existing maps app already does this reliably.
Multiple orders at once

A driver can be assigned more than one order if the shop is running [[del-multi-drop|multi-drop deliveries]], the app then shows a stacked list of stops in delivery order rather than a single card, and each stop is marked Delivered individually as the driver works through the round.
Troubleshooting

'The driver never got the notification for their order', first check the driver's phone isn't in Do Not Disturb or battery saver mode, both are known to suppress the push notification silently; the assignment still appears in-app if the driver opens it manually, so also check they simply haven't looked at the app since it's the notification that failed, not the assignment.

'Driver App shows a blank screen or won't load orders' is usually a stale session rather than a lost order, ask the driver to fully close and reopen the app rather than just backgrounding it; if it persists, see [[ts-driver-app-crash|the driver app crashing article]] for the fuller troubleshooting steps, including when to force a reinstall.

'Driver clocked in but doesn't show in Assign Driver on the terminal', this points to a shop mismatch, confirm the driver clocked in against the correct shop under Settings > Drivers rather than a different location they've also worked at, since the app defaults to whichever shop was last used.

'We want to stop a driver receiving new jobs without clocking them out entirely', use the Pause Driver toggle next to their name in Settings > Drivers > Manage Drivers, this keeps their shift clock running for pay purposes but removes them from the Assign Driver list until unpaused, useful for a driver on a break.
Overview

Delivery Zones define exactly which addresses and postcodes a shop will deliver to, and can carry different fees and minimum order values depending on distance from the shop. Getting zones set up correctly is the single biggest factor in avoiding the 'no takeaways in my postcode' complaint covered in [[ts-no-takeaways-in-postcode|the postcode coverage troubleshooting article]], since a badly drawn zone boundary is the most common root cause there.

Zones are configured under Settings > Delivery > Zones on the terminal (changes can also be made from the shop's web dashboard, which some owners find easier for drawing shapes on a map). A shop can run up to 6 zones at once on a Standard plan.
Drawing a zone

items: Zones can be drawn as a radius from the shop (e.g. a simple 3-mile circle) or as a custom polygon traced on the map, useful for excluding an area cut off by a dual carriageway or river even though it falls within a straight-line radius.
Each zone can have its own delivery fee and minimum order value, see the delivery fees article for how these combine with distance-based pricing.
Zones cannot overlap; if a new zone's boundary crosses an existing one, the terminal shows 'Overlaps with Zone 2' and won't save until the shapes are adjusted.
A postcode can be explicitly excluded even if it falls inside a zone's shape, using the Exclude Postcode option, useful for a single problem street with recurring access issues.
Zone changes take effect on the customer-facing site within around 10 minutes, existing orders already placed are unaffected.

blocks.caption: Delivery Zones map editor showing three overlapping-avoided zone shapes around the shop, colour-coded by delivery fee band, with the postcode exclusion list in the side panel.

blocks.text: Setting a maximum delivery distance

Beyond the outermost drawn zone, the shop simply doesn't appear as a delivery option at all, there's no automatic 'anything within X miles' fallback, every deliverable postcode must fall inside a defined zone. Shops that want to extend coverage temporarily (for example, a quiet Tuesday) can widen an existing zone rather than needing to create a new one each time.

Zone assignment also affects driver allocation when [[del-multi-drop|batching multiple orders onto one driver round]], since orders across two different zones on opposite sides of the shop are unlikely to be worth combining into a single trip even if a driver is free.
Troubleshooting

'A regular customer suddenly can't order anymore', check whether a zone boundary was recently redrawn narrower, often after a driver complains about a long or awkward drive, and the shop tightened the shape without realising it cut off an existing customer's street.

'Customers just inside our radius say we don't deliver to them', this is nearly always a polygon zone drawn slightly short of a true circular radius, since hand-drawn shapes rarely trace a perfect circle, walk the shop through re-drawing the affected edge under Settings > Delivery > Zones rather than assuming it's a system fault.

'We want higher delivery fees further out but the same zone', a single zone can only carry one flat fee, the shop needs to split it into two zones (e.g. a 0-2 mile zone and a 2-4 mile zone) to have fees step up with distance, see [[del-delivery-fees|how delivery fees are calculated]] for the maths behind zone-based fee bands.

'A customer paid but their address turned out to be outside our zone', this shouldn't be possible under normal operation since checkout blocks addresses outside all zones, if it happens, check whether the zone was edited after the order was placed, an edit doesn't retroactively cancel orders already in flight, so the order needs handling manually, potentially via [[ts-cancelling-accepted-order|the order cancellation process]] if the shop can't fulfil it.
Overview

Delivery fees are the charges passed on to the customer for having an order delivered, set by the shop rather than fixed by FMO, though FMO enforces some guardrails to keep pricing reasonable and consistent with [[mkt-minimum-discount|the minimum customer discount policy]] shops must also honour. Fees are configured per [[del-delivery-zones|delivery zone]], so a customer further from the shop can be charged more than one closer in.

Delivery fees are separate from, and not reduced by, any customer discount applied to the order itself, the minimum 3% discount applies only to the food and drink subtotal, never to the delivery fee or any service charge.
How a fee is calculated

items: Base fee: set per zone under Settings > Delivery > Zones > Fee, typically £1.50-£3.50 depending on distance band.

Small order surcharge: an optional extra fee (default £1.00) applied automatically when an order falls below the zone's minimum order value, configured under Settings > Delivery > Small Order Surcharge.

Peak surcharge: an optional percentage or flat top-up a shop can enable for known busy windows (e.g. Friday/Saturday 6pm-9pm), under Settings > Delivery > Peak Pricing, capped at a maximum 20% uplift on the base fee.

Free delivery threshold: shops can set an order value above which delivery becomes free (e.g. orders over £30), under Settings > Delivery > Free Delivery Threshold, this overrides both the base fee and any small order surcharge for that order.

blocks.caption: Delivery fee breakdown shown on an order receipt, listing the zone base fee, a peak surcharge line, and the free delivery threshold progress bar shown to the customer at checkout.

blocks.text: How the customer sees it

The delivery fee is shown to the customer at checkout before payment, broken down as a single line if only a base fee applies, or itemised if a peak or small-order surcharge is added, so a customer querying their receipt can be shown exactly why a fee was higher than they expected. This is worth checking before assuming a billing error, most 'why was I charged extra for delivery' calls resolve once the peak surcharge window is pointed out.

Delivery fees collected from customers flow into the shop's takings the same way order totals do, landing in [[sales-ap-funds|AP Funds]] immediately rather than being held back or paid out separately, and can be drawn on via [[sales-advantage-card|the Advantage Card]] like any other takings.
Troubleshooting

'Customer says they were charged delivery on an order that should have been free', check the order total against the Free Delivery Threshold setting, remembering the threshold applies to the food subtotal before any discount is deducted in some shop configurations but after it in others, check which mode the shop has selected under Settings > Delivery > Free Delivery Threshold > Calculation Basis.

'Delivery fee looks different to what's shown in the app description', the shop's public-facing delivery fee text (shown on their FMO shop page) is a static description and does not automatically update when the shop changes fees on the terminal, remind the shop to update this under Settings > Shop Profile > Delivery Info whenever pricing changes.

'We want to charge more for deliveries at night', this is exactly what Peak Pricing is for, walk the shop through Settings > Delivery > Peak Pricing and set a schedule rather than manually adjusting the base zone fee each evening and forgetting to change it back.

'A driver says the fee doesn't cover their trip', delivery fees fund the shop's operating costs generally rather than being paid directly to the driver per trip, driver earnings are calculated separately, see [[del-driver-pay|how driver pay is calculated]] for how that works.
Overview

A failed delivery is any order that a driver couldn't hand to the customer, whether because nobody answered the door, the address couldn't be found, or the customer refused the order on arrival. This article covers what Smart Link expects staff to do in each case and how refunds and re-deliveries are handled.

A driver marks a delivery as failed rather than delivered from the Driver App by tapping Report Issue on the active delivery card and selecting a reason, this is logged against the order immediately and surfaces on the terminal so staff don't need to wait for the driver to physically return to the shop before acting.
Failure reasons and what happens next

items: No Answer: the driver must attempt to call the customer's saved number (see the customer numbers article for which number that is) and wait a minimum of 5 minutes at the address before this reason can be selected.

Address Not Found: the order is flagged for staff to call the customer and confirm the address before redispatching, staff can use Edit Order to correct it if it was entered wrong at checkout, provided the order hasn't moved to Out for Delivery status changes that lock the address.
Customer Refused: the driver notes why (e.g. wrong item, item missing) and the order moves to a Refused queue for a manager decision on refund vs replacement.
Customer Unreachable at Door (present but unable to answer, e.g. flats with broken buzzers): treated the same as No Answer for refund purposes but flagged separately for driver safety reporting.

blocks.caption: Driver App Report Issue screen showing the four failure reason options with a note field and a photo-evidence upload button for the door or address.

blocks.text: Refunds and re-delivery

For No Answer and Address Not Found, the shop has 15 minutes from the failure being logged to decide between a re-delivery attempt (the order stays Out for Delivery and the same or a different driver retries) or a full refund, after which the terminal auto-refunds the customer to avoid the order sitting unresolved. For Customer Refused, no auto-refund timer applies since it usually needs a manual judgement call, similar to the process in [[ts-mistake-on-order|resolving a mistake on a customer's order]].

A driver who repeatedly logs failed deliveries against the same shop over a short period (3 or more in a single shift) triggers a flag visible to the shop owner under Settings > Drivers > Performance, intended to catch a genuine pattern early rather than penalise a single unlucky night.
Troubleshooting

'Customer says they were home the whole time', ask the driver for the photo evidence attached to the failure report if one was taken, and check the driver's last tracked position against the delivery address in [[hw-smart-link-tracking-drivers|the driver tracking screen]], a driver who never actually reached the address is a different problem to a genuine no-answer.

'The order still shows Out for Delivery even though it failed', a failure report should move the order out of that status automatically, if it hasn't, the driver's app may not have synced the report, check the Driver App is on a recent version and ask the driver to resubmit the report rather than manually marking it Delivered, which would incorrectly close the order without triggering the refund decision.

'We keep getting no-answer failures on Pre-Orders', check the customer's contact number was confirmed at booking, Pre-Orders taken well in advance are more likely to have a stale or mistyped number by the time delivery happens, staff should confirm the number again on the day if there's any doubt.

'Can we charge the customer again for a re-delivery attempt', no, a re-delivery attempt on the same order cannot carry an additional delivery fee, only a brand new order placed separately can be charged fresh fees.
Overview

Driver Pay is the system that calculates what a shop owes its drivers based on hours clocked and deliveries completed, tracked automatically from the same clock-in/clock-out and delivery data used by [[del-driver-app-overview|the Driver App]] and the driver tracking screen. FMO does not employ drivers directly, drivers work for the shop, so pay rules are configured by the shop within FMO's supported models rather than fixed centrally.

Driver Pay figures are for the shop's own payroll reference, FMO does not pay drivers directly on the shop's behalf, the shop still runs its own payroll or cash payments, Smart Link simply produces the numbers to make that easier and more accurate than manual timesheets.
Supported pay models

items: Hourly: a flat rate per clocked hour, configured under Settings > Drivers > Pay Model > Hourly Rate, the most common setup for shops running their own vehicles.
Per-delivery: a fixed amount per completed delivery regardless of distance, under Settings > Drivers > Pay Model > Per Delivery Rate, common for shops using drivers' own vehicles or bikes.

Per-delivery with distance banding: a base per-delivery rate plus an extra amount per mile beyond a threshold (e.g. £1.20 base, +15p per mile beyond 2 miles), under Settings > Drivers > Pay Model > Distance Banding.
Hybrid: a lower hourly retainer plus a smaller per-delivery top-up, intended for quieter shops that want to guarantee drivers a minimum income during slow periods.

blocks.caption: Driver Pay summary screen for a single driver showing clocked hours, completed deliveries, calculated pay under the shop's chosen model, and a weekly total.

blocks.text: Multi-drop and failed deliveries

Under per-delivery pay models, [[del-multi-drop|multi-drop rounds]] pay per stop delivered, not per round, so a driver completing a 3-stop round under a per-delivery model earns 3x the per-delivery rate, this is worth explaining clearly to new drivers who sometimes expect a single flat payment per trip out. A failed delivery (see the failed deliveries article) does not earn per-delivery pay unless the shop has separately enabled Pay on Attempt under Settings > Drivers > Pay Model > Failed Delivery Handling, which some shops use to compensate drivers for genuine no-answer situations outside their control.

Reports are exportable weekly from Settings > Drivers > Pay Reports as a CSV, useful for shops running payroll through third-party software, or handing to an accountant, the export includes a breakdown per driver per shift rather than just a weekly total.
Troubleshooting

'The pay total looks wrong for a driver who worked two shifts in one day', check whether the two shifts were clocked as separate sessions, some drivers forget to clock out at the end of a lunch shift and clock in again for evening, which the system reads as one long continuous shift and can distort hourly totals if the shop's rate changes between shifts.

'A driver disputes their delivery count', pull the full delivery list for the shift from Settings > Drivers > Pay Reports > [driver] > Shift Detail, which lists every order marked delivered under that driver's name with a timestamp, cross-reference against [[hw-smart-link-tracking-drivers|the tracking history]] if there's a genuine discrepancy.

'We changed our pay rate but old shifts recalculated too', pay rate changes only apply going forward from the moment they're saved, if historic shifts appear to have changed, check whether the report was regenerated after the rate change rather than the underlying shift data actually changing, the export always uses the rate in effect at the time of the shift.

'Can we set different rates for different drivers', yes, an individual driver's pay model and rate can be overridden from the shop-wide default under their profile in Settings > Drivers > Manage Drivers > [driver] > Pay Override, useful for a more experienced driver on a higher hourly rate.
Overview

Shops are responsible for making sure any driver delivering FMO orders is using a roadworthy, appropriately insured vehicle, FMO does not provide vehicles or insurance itself. This article sets out the baseline requirements shops should check before adding a driver in Settings > Drivers > Manage Drivers, and what documentation to keep on file.

These requirements apply regardless of vehicle type, car, moped, or bicycle, though the specific documents needed differ. A driver added to the terminal without valid documentation on file is still technically able to clock in via [[del-driver-app-overview|the Driver App]], Smart Link does not block this automatically, so it falls to the shop to enforce it before letting someone out on deliveries.
Minimum requirements by vehicle type

items: Car or moped: valid full driving licence for the vehicle class, business-use motor insurance (a standard social/domestic policy does not cover paid delivery work and is commonly the gap that invalidates a claim after an accident), and a MOT certificate if the vehicle is over 3 years old.
Moped/scooter specifically: CBT (Compulsory Basic Training) certificate as a minimum if riding on a provisional licence, plus a valid MOT once the vehicle is old enough to require one.
Bicycle: no licence or insurance is legally required, but shops are strongly encouraged to confirm the driver has basic public liability cover and a working set of lights for evening shifts.
All vehicle types: the shop should hold a legible copy of the driver's ID and, for car/moped, their licence and insurance certificate, on file for at least the duration the driver is active.

blocks.caption: Add Driver screen on the terminal showing the document upload fields for licence, insurance certificate and MOT, each marked with an expiry date field.

blocks.text: Document expiry tracking

When a shop uploads a driver's licence, insurance certificate or MOT date under Settings > Drivers > Manage Drivers > [driver] > Documents, Smart Link tracks the expiry date and shows an amber warning on the driver's profile 14 days before expiry, and a red warning once expired, though it does not automatically prevent an expired driver from clocking in, this is a prompt for the shop to act on, not an enforced block.

A shop found to be regularly running drivers without valid business-use insurance on file risks account review under the same process covered in [[acc-account-suspension|account suspension]], since it represents a meaningful liability and safety risk both to the shop and to FMO's reputation.
Troubleshooting

'A driver's documents show as expired but they're still working', the expiry warning is informational only, remind the shop owner it's their responsibility to stand a driver down until updated documents are uploaded, Smart Link will keep showing the warning but won't remove the driver from the Assign Driver list on its own.

'We can't find where to upload a new insurance certificate after renewal', it's under the same driver's profile, Settings > Drivers > Manage Drivers > [driver] > Documents > Insurance, uploading a new certificate with a later expiry date automatically clears the warning.

'Do bicycle couriers need to go through the same document upload flow', no, the Documents tab adapts based on the vehicle type selected when the driver was added, bicycle-only drivers see just an optional public liability field rather than the full licence/insurance/MOT set.

'A customer complained about a driver's vehicle condition', this is a shop-side matter to address directly with the driver, but if it recurs it's worth logging via a support ticket referencing the driver's profile so it's visible if the shop later needs the history during an account review.
Overview

Multi-drop deliveries let a shop send one driver out with more than one order at a time, batched into a single round, rather than dispatching a separate driver per order. This is most useful during busy periods when several orders in similar directions are ready around the same time, and can meaningfully cut down on driver idle time between trips.

Multi-drop is opt-in per shop, enabled under Settings > Delivery > Multi-Drop, and off by default, since it isn't suitable for every shop, particularly ones with a small delivery radius where trips are already short.
How batching works

items: Orders are only suggested for batching if they fall within the same delivery zone (see the delivery zones article) and are ready within a configurable window of each other, default 10 minutes.
Staff assigning a driver see a 'Batch with [Order #]' suggestion on the order card when a compatible order is also ready, but batching is never automatic, a staff member must confirm it.
A maximum of 4 orders can be batched into a single round on a Standard plan, configurable down (not up) under Settings > Delivery > Multi-Drop > Max Drops.
The terminal calculates a suggested drop order based on route efficiency, but staff or the driver can reorder stops manually if local knowledge suggests a better route.

blocks.caption: Assign Driver screen showing a batching suggestion prompt linking two ready orders in the same zone, with a suggested stop order shown beneath.

blocks.text: How it appears to drivers and customers

On [[del-driver-app-overview|the Driver App]], a batched round appears as a stacked list of stops rather than a single delivery card, and each stop is marked Delivered individually as the driver works through them, the overall order only leaves Out for Delivery status once its specific stop is completed, not when the whole round finishes.

Customers on a multi-drop round see a slightly wider estimated arrival window than a single-order delivery would show, to account for the driver making other stops first, this is intentional and not a fault if a customer queries why their estimate looks longer than usual.
Troubleshooting

'Two orders were batched but they're on completely different sides of town', check the zone boundaries under [[del-delivery-zones|delivery zones]], a zone drawn too widely (e.g. a single large radius rather than several smaller ones) can suggest batching for orders that are technically in-zone but not actually close together, narrowing the zones usually fixes the suggestion quality.

'A customer's order arrived much later than expected on a multi-drop round', check the stop order the driver actually followed against the suggested route, if a driver reorders stops for convenience it can push a customer further back than the system intended, this is worth a quiet word with the driver rather than a system fix.

'Driver pay looks low for a multi-drop shift', under per-delivery pay models each stop pays individually, see [[del-driver-pay|driver pay]] for how that's calculated, if a driver expected a bundled higher rate for taking on multiple stops at once, check whether the shop intends to offer a multi-drop bonus, which needs configuring separately as a manual pay override rather than being automatic.

'We want to turn batching off just for weekends', there's no scheduled toggle for Multi-Drop currently, it's a single on/off setting, a shop wanting this needs to manually toggle it under Settings > Delivery > Multi-Drop at the relevant times.
Overview

Know Your Customer (KYC) checks are the identity and business verification steps every shop must pass before its FMO account can go live, and periodically thereafter. They exist to satisfy FMO's obligations under UK anti-money laundering regulations and card scheme rules, and they sit alongside the document requirements covered during [[sales-signing-up-new-shop|new shop sign-up]]. Staff should treat KYC as a compliance gate rather than a formality, an account cannot process live orders or hold a balance in [[sales-ap-funds|AP Funds]] until it clears.

KYC is carried out by the Accounts team using documents submitted through the Partner App, and applies both to new shops going live and to existing shops making certain changes, such as an ownership change (see [[sales-updating-shop-details|updating shop details]]) or a change to the bank account linked to the Advantage Card.
What gets checked

items: Identity of at least one director or the sole trader/partner, verified against a passport or UK driving licence.
Proof of address for that individual, dated within the last 3 months (utility bill, bank statement, or council tax letter).
Business registration details, Companies House number for limited companies, or HMRC self-assessment reference for sole traders.
Bank account ownership, the account name on the linked bank account must match the registered business name or the verified individual's name.
A basic sanctions and PEP (politically exposed person) screening check, run automatically against the submitted identity details.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the Partner App verification screen showing document upload slots for photo ID, proof of address, and business registration, each with a pending, approved or rejected status badge.

blocks.text: Timescales and outcomes

Most submissions are reviewed within 1-2 working days of all documents being uploaded. If a document is unclear, expired, or doesn't match the name on the account, the submission is marked 'Needs Attention' in the Partner App with a specific reason, rather than a blanket rejection, so the shop knows exactly what to resubmit. Accounts will not approve a partial submission and wait for the rest to trickle in, the whole set is reviewed together.

A shop that fails KYC outright (for example, a sanctions match, or documents that appear altered) is referred to Trust & Safety rather than simply asked to resubmit, and the account is held in a suspended state pending manual review, see [[acc-account-suspension|account suspension]] for what that means day to day.
Re-verification

Existing shops are not re-verified on a fixed schedule, but certain triggers force a re-check: a change of registered business name, a change of linked bank account, a new director being added on Companies House, or a chargeback rate that crosses the review threshold described in [[acc-chargebacks|the chargebacks article]]. When re-verification is triggered, the shop's Partner App will show a banner prompting fresh document upload; the account is not suspended purely for a re-verification request unless documents aren't provided within 14 days.
Troubleshooting

'Why do you need my personal ID, this is a business account', a common question from limited company owners. Explain that at least one natural person behind any business account must be verified under FMO's AML obligations, this is a regulatory requirement rather than an FMO preference, and applies to every partner regardless of company size.

'I uploaded my documents three days ago and heard nothing', check the Partner App submission status first, if it shows 'Needs Attention' the shop likely missed an in-app notification about a specific document issue; if it genuinely shows 'Pending Review' beyond 3 working days, escalate to Accounts rather than asking the shop to resubmit unnecessarily.

'My bank account is in my personal name but the business is a limited company', this is a common rejection reason, the account name must match either the verified individual or the registered business name exactly; a personal account can only be used if that individual is a verified director, otherwise a business bank account is required.

'Can I go live while verification is still pending', no, this mirrors the rule during onboarding, an account cannot accept live orders until verification clears, since this is also what enables card payments to settle into [[sales-ap-funds|the shop's AP Funds balance]] in the first place.
Overview

Every FMO shop handles customer personal data, names, addresses, phone numbers and order history, captured through features like [[customer-numbers-multiple|Customer Numbers]] and [[mkt-sms-sending-campaign|SMS marketing campaigns]]. FMO is the data controller for information collected through the app and website, but shops act as a data processor for certain functions carried out on Smart Link, such as adding notes to a customer profile or storing a customer's preferred delivery instructions. This article sets out what shops are and aren't allowed to do with that data under UK GDPR.

Support staff fielding data protection questions should treat this as a compliance matter, not a product how-to, if a shop's question goes beyond what's covered here, escalate to Trust & Safety rather than guessing.
What shops can and can't do

items: Shops can view and use customer contact details for the purpose of fulfilling an order, including calling a customer back about a query on that order.

Shops cannot export customer phone numbers or addresses in bulk for use outside FMO (e.g. into a separate marketing tool); all SMS marketing must go through [[mkt-sms-sending-campaign|the built-in SMS campaign feature]], which enforces opt-out compliance automatically.
Shops cannot contact a customer for anything unrelated to an order or a campaign the customer has opted into, this includes unsolicited calls asking for reviews outside FMO's own review flow.
Staff accounts must not be shared between employees; each staff member should have their own login so actions are attributable, see [[acc-multi-user-access|multi-user access]] for how to set this up.
Customer data must not be retained or copied onto personal devices, printed order slips containing customer details should be disposed of securely, not left on the counter or bin at end of shift.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the Data & Privacy settings page showing the shop's data processing agreement status, staff access log, and a Request Data Export button restricted to the account owner.

blocks.text: Customer data requests

Customers have the right to request a copy of their data or ask for it to be deleted under UK GDPR. If a shop receives such a request directly (rather than the customer using the app's built-in privacy settings), it should be forwarded to dataprotection@fmo internally rather than actioned by the shop itself, since deletion has knock-on effects for order history and refund records that need to be handled centrally.

Order data is retained for 6 years for tax and dispute purposes even after a customer requests deletion of their profile, this is a legal retention requirement rather than an FMO choice, and applies consistently across all shops. This is also why a customer number cannot always be fully removed from a profile within the 90-day window described in the Customer Numbers article.
Data breaches

If a shop suspects customer data has been exposed, for example a lost staff device that was logged into Smart Link, or a staff member emailing an order list to a personal account, this must be reported to Trust & Safety immediately, not held until the next scheduled check-in. FMO has a regulatory obligation to assess and, where required, report qualifying breaches to the ICO within 72 hours, so delays at the shop level directly affect FMO's ability to meet that deadline.
Troubleshooting

'A customer is asking us directly to delete their data, what do we do', do not attempt to delete anything from the shop side, forward the request to dataprotection@fmo and let the customer know it's being handled, deletion touches systems shops don't have access to.

'Can we keep a spreadsheet of regular customers' numbers for our own records', no, this falls outside what shops are authorised to do with customer data under the processing agreement, all customer contact should stay within Smart Link's Customer Numbers and campaign tools.

'One of our staff left and we think they still have access', this is a multi-user access issue as much as a data one, remove the staff login immediately under [[acc-multi-user-access|Multi-User Access]], and if there's any suggestion they took customer data with them, log it as a potential breach with Trust & Safety.

'A customer says a competitor called them using their FMO order details', treat this as a serious report, not a routine complaint, escalate directly to Trust & Safety with the order reference and timeline, this is the kind of pattern that triggers a wider investigation across the shop's staff access log.
Overview

A chargeback happens when a customer disputes a card payment directly with their bank rather than raising the issue with the shop or FMO support, common triggers include 'I didn't receive my order', 'this wasn't authorised by me', or a duplicate charge like the ones described in [[ts-payment-taken-order-declined|Payment Taken but Order Declined]]. Chargebacks are handled by Payments Ops and follow the card networks' own dispute timelines, which are considerably slower and more formal than a normal refund.

Unlike a standard refund, a chargeback pulls the disputed amount back from the shop's [[sales-ap-funds|AP Funds]] balance immediately once the bank raises it, before the dispute is even resolved, along with a £15 chargeback administration fee. If the dispute is won by the shop, both the original amount and the fee are returned; if lost, neither is.
How the process runs

items: The customer's bank notifies the card network, which notifies FMO, this typically arrives 5-35 days after the original transaction, sometimes longer.
The disputed amount and £15 fee are deducted from AP Funds the same day the dispute is received, showing as a 'Chargeback Hold' line in Payments > Transaction History.
The shop is notified via the Partner App and has 7 days to submit evidence (proof of delivery, order confirmation, driver tracking log) if it wants to contest the dispute.
Payments Ops submits the shop's evidence to the card network, which typically takes 30-45 days to issue a ruling, occasionally longer for card-network-level escalations.
If the shop wins, funds and the fee are returned to AP Funds within 5 business days of the ruling; if the shop loses, the hold becomes a permanent deduction.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the Payments > Chargebacks tab showing a disputed order with its status (Evidence Submitted), the amount on hold, and a countdown to the evidence submission deadline.

blocks.text: Chargeback rate and account risk

FMO monitors each shop's chargeback rate as a percentage of total card transactions over a rolling 30-day window. A rate above 0.65% triggers an automated warning to the shop; a rate above 1% triggers a mandatory review by Trust & Safety and can result in tighter Text to Pay limits or, in persistent cases, contribute to [[acc-account-suspension|account suspension]]. A high chargeback rate is also one of the triggers for re-verification under [[acc-kyc-verification|KYC checks]].

The single biggest driver of avoidable chargebacks is poor communication about order changes, this is why using Edit Order and keeping delivery notes accurate matters, a customer who feels blindsided by a substitution is far more likely to dispute the charge than call the shop first.
Troubleshooting

'Money's just disappeared from our AP Funds balance and we don't know why', check Payments > Chargebacks first before escalating as a payments fault, a chargeback hold is applied automatically and silently reduces the visible balance, it isn't a system error.

'The customer says they never disputed anything', this does happen, sometimes a cardholder disputes a transaction they don't recognise on their statement without realising it relates to a legitimate FMO order; encourage the shop to still submit evidence, a chargeback can be reversed even if it was raised in error by the customer.

'We submitted evidence, why hasn't the money come back yet', the 30-45 day card network ruling window is fixed and cannot be expedited by FMO, this needs managing as an expectation with the shop rather than escalated repeatedly to Payments Ops.

'Can we just refund the customer ourselves to stop a chargeback happening', yes, if a shop spots a legitimate complaint early, issuing a proactive refund through Payments > Adjustments before the customer's bank gets involved avoids the £15 fee entirely and is the recommended approach whenever a dispute looks likely.
Overview

Account suspension takes a shop offline, removed from customer search results and unable to accept new orders on Smart Link, while a specific issue is investigated or resolved. It's a serious step and distinct from a shop simply toggling itself to 'Closed' under Menu Availability, a suspended shop cannot bring itself back online, only Trust & Safety or Account Management can lift a suspension.

Suspension is not the same as a warning. Most issues are handled with a notice period and a chance to fix the underlying problem first, suspension is reserved for cases with immediate risk to customers, payments integrity, or FMO's own regulatory position.
Common causes

items: Failing or refusing to complete [[acc-kyc-verification|KYC verification]], or a sanctions/PEP match found during screening.
A chargeback rate persistently above 1% over a rolling 30-day window with no improvement after a formal warning, see [[acc-chargebacks|chargebacks]].
A serious food hygiene or allergen incident, particularly one involving a confirmed allergic reaction, see [[acc-allergen-info|allergen responsibilities]].
A confirmed data protection breach involving customer information, as described in [[acc-data-protection|data protection]].
Non-payment of subscription or commission fees beyond the grace period set out in [[sales-subscription-commission|subscription and commission]].
Evidence of fraudulent order activity, such as staff processing fake orders to draw down [[sales-ap-funds|AP Funds]] or misuse of [[request-funds-same-day|same-day fund requests]].

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the Partner App home screen for a suspended account, showing a red banner reading 'Account Suspended - Contact Account Management', with ordering and payment features greyed out.

blocks.text: What happens during suspension

The shop's listing is removed from customer search immediately, existing accepted orders in progress are allowed to complete normally so customers aren't left without their food, but no new orders can be taken. AP Funds balance remains visible but withdrawals via Request Funds or the Advantage Card are frozen until the suspension is lifted, this protects against a shop drawing down funds while an issue (particularly a chargeback or fraud concern) is still being investigated.

A suspended shop is contacted directly by Trust & Safety or Account Management (depending on the cause) within 1 working day, explaining the reason and what's needed for reinstatement. Support staff taking an inbound call from a suspended shop should not attempt to explain the specific reason unless it's already visible in the account notes, and should instead confirm the shop has been contacted and direct them to respond to that outreach.
Reinstatement

Reinstatement timelines vary by cause: a KYC-related suspension typically clears within 1-2 working days of corrected documents being submitted, a chargeback-related suspension requires a documented plan (often 30 days of monitoring at a reduced Text to Pay limit) before full restoration, and a fraud or serious hygiene/allergen suspension goes through a formal review that can take 2-4 weeks. There is no self-service reinstatement, a shop cannot lift its own suspension no matter the cause.
Troubleshooting

'We've gone offline and nobody's called us', check the account notes for the suspension reason and the date it was applied, if it's been more than 1 working day with no outreach logged, escalate to Account Management directly rather than telling the shop to keep waiting.

'Our money is stuck and we need it for wages', explain clearly that AP Funds withdrawals are frozen for the duration of a suspension regardless of the reason, this isn't negotiable at first line, but flag urgent hardship cases to Account Management, who can occasionally arrange a partial release for verified payroll needs.

'We fixed the issue days ago but we're still suspended', ask the shop what evidence they submitted and when, then check whether it reached the right team, a document uploaded to the wrong place (e.g. general support instead of the KYC resubmission flow) can sit unreviewed.

'Can we just sign up as a new shop instead of waiting', no, attempting to re-register the same business or the same individual under a new account while a suspension is active is itself treated as an aggravating factor during review, and will be flagged during [[acc-kyc-verification|verification]] on the new application.
Overview

UK law requires food businesses to display their Food Hygiene Rating Scheme (FHRS) sticker in Scotland and Wales, and it's recommended practice in England; FMO goes further and shows the rating on the shop's customer-facing FMO profile everywhere in the UK, since it's one of the biggest factors customers weigh before ordering. This is separate from the shop's own [[mkt-customer-reviews|customer reviews]], which reflect food quality and service rather than hygiene inspection outcomes.
