Ratings themselves are set by the local authority, not FMO, following an inspection, FMO only displays whatever rating is publicly recorded against the shop's registered address on the Food Standards Agency (FSA) database.
How the rating gets onto a shop's FMO profile

items: During [[sales-signing-up-new-shop|shop sign-up]], the onboarding team looks up the shop's FHRS rating using the registered business address and links it to the account.
The rating syncs automatically from the FSA's public database on a monthly refresh, so a shop that's recently been re-inspected should see an updated score within roughly 4-6 weeks.
A shop can request an earlier manual refresh via Settings > Business > Food Hygiene Rating > Request Update, if a new inspection result is out but hasn't synced yet.

If a shop moves premises, this must be reported through [[sales-updating-shop-details|updating shop details]], since the rating is tied to the address, not the business, and a new address means a fresh inspection and a fresh rating until inspected.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of a shop's customer-facing FMO profile page showing the Food Hygiene Rating badge (5 - Very Good) next to the shop name, with a 'Last verified' date beneath it.

blocks.text: Low or missing ratings

A shop rated 0-2 by the local authority is still permitted to trade legally, but FMO displays a clear low-rating badge rather than hiding it, since customers are entitled to make an informed choice; shops should not ask support to remove or obscure a genuinely low rating. A shop that has never been inspected (common for very new premises) shows as 'Awaiting Inspection' rather than no badge at all.

If a shop believes its displayed rating is wrong or out of date compared to what the local authority has on file, the fix is always at the source, the shop should contact its local authority or check the FSA website directly, FMO cannot override a rating manually even temporarily, since it would misrepresent an inspection outcome.
Troubleshooting

'We were re-inspected last month and got a 5, but the app still shows our old 3', this is almost always the monthly sync lag, confirm the new rating is live on the FSA website first, then use Request Update rather than waiting for the next automatic refresh.

'Our rating badge has disappeared completely', check whether the shop recently went through [[sales-updating-shop-details|an address change]], the badge resets to 'Awaiting Inspection' at a new premises until the local authority carries out a fresh visit, this is expected, not a bug.

'A customer is threatening to leave a bad review because of our hygiene rating', this is a review matter, not a hygiene rating matter, point staff to [[mkt-customer-reviews|the customer reviews article]] for how reviews are handled, FMO cannot adjust the displayed rating regardless of review pressure.

'Can we hide the rating while we wait for a re-inspection appeal', no, the FHRS rating displayed is always whatever is current on the FSA database, an appeal in progress does not change what's shown until the appeal concludes and the record updates.
Overview

Under UK food information regulations (Natasha's Law and the wider Food Information Regulations), shops must be able to provide accurate allergen information for every item on their menu, covering the 14 legally recognised allergens. FMO builds allergen fields into the menu setup process covered during [[sales-signing-up-new-shop|sign-up]], but keeping that information accurate day to day is the shop's ongoing legal responsibility, not FMO's.

This is one of the few areas where a shop's own error can trigger [[acc-account-suspension|account suspension]] directly and quickly, particularly where a customer suffers a confirmed allergic reaction, so it's worth treating allergen questions from shops with real seriousness rather than routing them as a generic menu query.
Setting up allergen information

items: Each menu item must have all 14 allergens explicitly marked as Contains, Does Not Contain, or May Contain (for cross-contamination risk), a blank field is not accepted at menu setup.
Allergen data is entered under Settings > Menu > Allergens, at the product level, variants (e.g. different bases, sauces) can carry different allergen profiles from their parent product.
A menu item cannot be published live with incomplete allergen data, the system blocks it in the same way [[menu-availability|Menu Availability]] blocks checkout on an unavailable item.
Shops should re-review allergen data whenever a recipe or supplier ingredient changes, this is a shop process responsibility and isn't something FMO can detect automatically.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the Menu Editor's Allergens tab for a single product, showing all 14 allergens listed with Contains/May Contain/Does Not Contain selectors and a warning banner for two unmarked allergens.

blocks.text: How this reaches the customer

Allergen information set here is shown to customers on the item page before ordering, and is also the information used if a customer messages the shop directly with a specific allergy question through the app. If a customer places an order and adds a free-text note asking about an allergen (rather than checking the listed information), staff must still answer directly and accurately, the printed order note referenced in [[pf-order-notes|Order Notes]] is a good place to confirm this was communicated back.
Incidents

Any report of an allergic reaction linked to an FMO order, confirmed or suspected, must be escalated to Trust & Safety the same day, with the order reference, the allergen in question, and what the menu listing said at the time. This is treated with the same urgency as a data breach report, delayed reporting is itself treated as an aggravating factor if the incident is later reviewed.
Troubleshooting

'We can't publish a new menu item, it says allergen info is incomplete', check every one of the 14 allergen fields individually rather than assuming a bulk 'safe' default exists, there isn't one, every allergen must be explicitly set even if the honest answer is Does Not Contain.

'A customer says we told them wrong allergen information over the phone', pull the order note history and any recorded chat, and escalate to Trust & Safety regardless of whether a reaction occurred, near-miss reports matter for pattern tracking across shops.

'Our supplier changed an ingredient and we forgot to update the listing', advise the shop to correct it immediately via Settings > Menu > Allergens and, if any orders went out in the meantime with wrong information, to proactively flag this to Trust & Safety rather than wait to see if a complaint comes in.

'Do variants need their own allergen info or do they inherit from the main product', variants must be checked individually, a 'Gluten Free Base' variant, for example, needs its own allergen profile distinct from the standard base, inheriting the parent product's data is a common and serious setup mistake.
Overview

Multi-User Access lets a shop set up individual staff logins on Smart Link rather than everyone sharing one account password, so actions like accepting orders, editing prices, or requesting funds can be attributed to a specific person. This matters operationally (see [[my-orders-incoming|My Orders]] for how multiple devices can be logged in at once) and matters for compliance, since shared logins make it impossible to properly investigate a [[acc-data-protection|data protection]] concern or a disputed [[edit-order-updating|order edit]].

Every shop account has one Owner login created at [[sales-signing-up-new-shop|sign-up]], which cannot be deleted or downgraded, additional staff logins are created and managed by the Owner or an Admin-level user underneath it.
Permission levels

items: Owner: full access including bank details, Advantage Card, subscription and billing, and adding/removing other users, one per account.
Admin: full day-to-day access (orders, menu, marketing, staff management) but cannot change bank details or close the account.
Staff: can accept/decline orders, use Edit Order, and take payments, but cannot access Settings > Payments, Menu pricing, or any user management screens.
Kitchen: view-only access to incoming orders and Menu Availability toggles (for marking items sold out), used on devices kept in food prep areas away from payments.

blocks.caption: Screenshot of the Staff Access settings page listing four staff logins with their permission level badges (Admin, Staff, Staff, Kitchen) and a 'Last active' timestamp for each.

blocks.text: Setting up and removing staff logins

New logins are created under Settings > Staff > Add User, entering the staff member's name, mobile number (used for login verification via SMS code) and permission level. There's no fixed limit on the number of staff logins a shop can create, this scales with the size of the operation, larger multi-site groups covered under [[sales-multi-site-accounts|multi-site accounts]] typically run considerably more logins than a single shop.

When a staff member leaves, their login should be removed the same day under Settings > Staff > Remove User, rather than left dormant, a dormant login is both a security risk and makes the staff activity log harder to read when investigating an issue later. Removing a login does not delete the historical record of actions that person took, those remain attributed to them for audit purposes.
Troubleshooting

'We don't know who processed a refund', check Settings > Staff > Activity Log, every payment adjustment, order edit and menu change is timestamped against the specific login that made it, provided staff aren't sharing logins in the first place.

'A staff member left weeks ago and we forgot to remove them', remove the login immediately and, if there's any indication the account was used after they left (check the Activity Log timestamps against their known leaving date), treat this as a potential [[acc-data-protection|data protection]] concern and flag it to Trust & Safety.

'Can Kitchen-level staff take payments in an emergency', no, Kitchen access deliberately excludes payments and settings screens, if a shop needs broader access on a kitchen device, they should assign a Staff-level login there instead rather than working around the restriction.

'We want one login everyone uses because it's quicker', this should be actively discouraged, shared logins undermine the audit trail needed for chargeback evidence, allergen incident review, and general account security, and support should explain the risk rather than simply accommodating the request.
Overview

Order Notes is the free-text field customers can fill in at checkout to pass on a request that doesn't fit neatly into the standard ordering flow, things like 'no onions please', 'ring the bell, don't knock', or a flat/gate buzzer code. It sits below the basket summary on the customer-facing checkout page and is entirely optional, most orders arrive with it blank.

Because a note is free text rather than a structured field, it's not the same as a dietary or allergy declaration made against a specific item, see [[acc-allergen-info|the Allergen Information article]] for how those are captured separately and why staff shouldn't rely on a note alone for anything safety-critical.
Where notes appear and print

items: A note is limited to 200 characters and is stripped of links and phone numbers automatically, customers cannot use it to share a callback number outside the platform.
Notes print on both the kitchen copy and the delivery copy of the order ticket, directly beneath the item list, so kitchen and driver-facing staff both see the same wording.

If a note contains a recognised allergy keyword ('nut', 'gluten', 'dairy', 'shellfish' and common variants), the ticket prints with a bold amber 'CHECK NOTE' banner across the top rather than relying on staff to spot it in a paragraph of free text.

Notes on a Pre-Order print at the same point the order activates into the live queue, not at the time it was originally placed, see [[pre-orders-how-they-work|the Pre-Orders article]] for how that activation timing works.
A basic profanity filter blocks a note from being submitted if it contains flagged language, the customer sees 'Please rephrase your note' rather than the order failing silently.

blocks.caption: Order ticket showing an Order Note printed beneath the item list, with the amber CHECK NOTE banner triggered by an allergy keyword.

blocks.text: Acting on a note after acceptance

A note itself can't be edited by the shop, it belongs to the customer's original checkout, but if a note reveals something that needs a change to the order (for example, an allergy note means an ingredient needs removing), staff should make that change through [[edit-order-updating|Edit Order]] rather than just verbally telling the kitchen, so the change is logged against the order and the customer gets the automatic notification.

Notes also show on the order card in [[my-orders-incoming|My Orders]] itself, in a small expandable strip under the customer's name, so staff reviewing the queue don't need to wait for the printed ticket to see a note before deciding whether to accept.
What Order Notes can't be used for

items: Requesting a discount or price change, this must go through Payments > Manual Adjustment if genuinely warranted, not be actioned off the back of a note.

Changing the delivery address or requested time, these are structured fields and a note referencing a different address is ignored by the system and should be treated as a red flag worth a phone call.

Guaranteeing an item substitution, a note asking for a swap only reaches staff once the order prints, it doesn't check stock or [[menu-availability|Menu Availability]] automatically, so an unavailable substitution still needs manual handling.

blocks.text: Troubleshooting

"A customer says they added a note but the shop says the ticket was blank", check whether the order printed before the note was saved, a note added in the final seconds of checkout on a slow connection can occasionally miss the print job that already fired; pull the order in Order Lookup, the note will still be visible there even if it didn't make the physical ticket, and staff can read it out to the kitchen manually.

"The shop ignored an allergy note and it caused a real problem", this is treated as a priority issue rather than a standard complaint, escalate immediately in line with the allergy handling guidance in [[ts-mistake-on-order|Resolving a Mistake on a Customer's Order]] rather than working it as a routine Order Notes ticket.

"Can we reply to a customer's note?", no, Order Notes is one-directional from customer to shop, if the shop needs to ask a clarifying question they should call the customer on the number shown on the order rather than expecting a reply channel through the note field.

"Our note field on the terminal looks empty even though the customer says they wrote one", check the note isn't sitting collapsed under the small 'Note' chevron on the order card in My Orders, this is the single most common cause reported, staff assume a blank field rather than an unexpanded one.
Overview

AP Smart Link's software is kept current through over-the-air (OTA) firmware updates rather than anything a shop has to download or install manually. Updates are pushed centrally, tested internally, then rolled out in stages, and cover everything from new features (see [[whats-new-in-smartlink|What's New in Smart Link]] for a running log of what's shipped) to security patches for the built-in card payment module.

Firmware and the Smart Link app itself are versioned together as a single build number, shown under Settings > About > Software Version, in the form 4.x.x. Staff should always read this number back during a support call, since a number of fixes only apply from a specific build onward.
How the rollout works

items: Updates are pushed overnight between 2am and 5am UK time in almost all cases, to avoid interrupting live trading.
Larger or higher-risk releases go out in rings: a small percentage of terminals first (ring 1), then a wider group a few days later if no issues are reported, then everyone else.
A terminal checks for a pending update automatically once a day; staff can also force a check manually via Settings > System > Check for Updates.

Auto Update can be paused temporarily under Settings > System > Auto Update, some shops do this deliberately during a known busy period to avoid a mid-service reboot, but it should be re-enabled afterwards rather than left off long-term.

blocks.caption: Settings > System > Auto Update screen showing the current build number, last update check time, and the Check for Updates button.

blocks.text: Minimum supported builds

Terminals are expected to stay reasonably current. Builds below 4.9.0 are considered out of support for new feature requests, and from time to time a hard cutoff is enforced for compliance reasons, most notably around the card payment module referenced in [[hw-smart-link-card-payments|the card payments article]], where PCI requirements mean an unsupported build can be blocked from processing new transactions until it updates. A shop on a very old build calling in about a missing feature should be advised to update rather than have the feature investigated as a bug.

A full update typically installs within 10-15 minutes overnight with no shop-side action needed. If a shop reports the terminal was slow or unavailable first thing in the morning, check whether an update was mid-install by looking at the update history under Settings > System > Update History.
Manual checks and forcing an update

If a shop needs a fix urgently and doesn't want to wait for the overnight window, a manual check via Settings > System > Check for Updates will pull down any update the terminal is eligible for immediately, though this does mean a short reboot during the day, so it's worth warning the shop before triggering it during service.
Troubleshooting

"My terminal froze after the update", the standard first step is a full power-off, holding the power button for 10 seconds, rather than a soft restart, since a soft restart can leave an update half-applied. If it boots to a black screen with a spinning dot for more than 5 minutes, log a hardware ticket rather than continuing to troubleshoot in shop.

"The update keeps failing and retrying", this shows as error code FW-07 on screen. It usually means the terminal lost its network connection mid-download, check [[hw-smart-link-connectivity|the connectivity troubleshooting article]] first, as an unstable connection is by far the most common cause. The terminal will retry automatically up to 3 times before giving up and needing a manual retry.

"Can we roll back to the old version, we preferred it", not shop-side. A rollback is possible in exceptional cases (for example, a critical bug affecting order intake) but has to be actioned by the Hardware team centrally within a 7-day window of the release, it isn't a self-service option and shouldn't be promised to a shop as something support can arrange directly.

"Two shops on the same street are on different versions", this is expected during a staged ring rollout and isn't a fault, both terminals will converge on the same build within a few days as the rollout completes.
Overview

Loyalty Points is an optional scheme shops can switch on to reward repeat ordering, sitting alongside, not instead of, the platform-wide minimum discount described in [[mkt-minimum-discount|the minimum discount article]]. Customers earn points automatically on every order and can redeem them for money off a future order, giving shops another lever to bring lapsed customers back without running a full discount campaign each time.

Unlike the 3% minimum discount, Loyalty Points is entirely optional and off by default, a shop switches it on from Marketing > Loyalty > Enable Loyalty Points, and it costs nothing extra beyond the standard subscription referenced in [[sales-subscription-commission|the subscription and commission article]], redemptions simply come off the shop's own order value the same way any discount does.
How points are earned and redeemed

items: Customers earn 1 point per £1 spent on the food/drink subtotal, delivery charges don't earn points.
Points are credited automatically once an order is marked Accepted, not at checkout, so a declined order never earns points.
100 points redeem for £3 off a future order; redemption is all-or-nothing per order, customers can't part-redeem a points balance.
Points expire after 12 months of no activity on the account (no new order and no redemption), a shop can't shorten or extend this window itself.
Loyalty Points and the minimum 3% discount both apply to the same order without conflict, they're calculated independently, one off the subtotal, one from the customer's points balance.

blocks.caption: Marketing > Loyalty dashboard showing points earned this month, redemptions, and the current 1 point per £1 earn rate.

blocks.text: Boosting participation

Shops running a [[mkt-downtime-promotions|Downtime Promotion]] can optionally set a temporary points multiplier for that same window, for example double points Monday-Thursday 2:30pm-5pm, which stacks nicely with an already-quiet period incentive. A points balance reminder can also be worked into an [[mkt-sms-sending-campaign|SMS campaign]], since 'you have 340 points, that's £9 off your next order' tends to perform better than a generic reminder message.

Loyalty Points has no bearing on a shop's ranking or reviews, that's driven separately by the factors covered in [[mkt-customer-reviews|the Customer Reviews article]], but shops with an active scheme often see a modest lift in review volume simply from higher repeat-order frequency.
Reporting

Marketing > Loyalty > Performance shows total points issued, redeemed, and expired over any date range, along with an estimate of incremental repeat orders attributable to redemptions, useful for a shop weighing up whether to keep the scheme running.
Troubleshooting

"A customer says their points disappeared", check the account's last order or redemption date, if it's over 12 months, the points expired as expected; this is the single most common Loyalty Points complaint and there's no manual reinstatement available for expired points.

"We turned Loyalty Points on but customers say they're not earning anything", confirm the order actually reached Accepted status, a Pending or Declined order never credits points, and check the scheme wasn't switched on partway through the day, since points only accrue on orders placed after activation, not retroactively.

"Can a customer redeem points on the same order they're also using the FMO Movement donation toggle on?", yes, the two are independent, a customer can redeem points for money off and still choose to donate their standing discount on the same order, they aren't mutually exclusive.

"We want to change the earn rate to 2 points per £1", the standard 1 point per £1 rate is fixed platform-wide for consistency in how it's marketed to customers, a shop wanting a different rate should raise it with Account Management as a request rather than expect to change it themselves in Settings.
Overview

Seasonal Campaigns is a planning tool that helps shops line up their marketing around predictable, high-demand dates in the UK calendar, Christmas, New Year, Valentine's Day, Pancake Day, Mother's Day, Easter, big football fixtures, Bonfire Night, Halloween, and Black Friday among others, rather than reacting to them at the last minute.

It doesn't replace the standard tools covered elsewhere, a seasonal campaign is really just an [[mkt-sms-sending-campaign|SMS campaign]] and, optionally, a time-limited discount, planned against a known date with a recommended lead time built in, so shops aren't sending a Valentine's message on Valentine's Day itself when most orders have already been decided.
Using the Seasonal Planner

items: Marketing > Campaigns > Seasonal Planner lists upcoming key dates for the next 90 days, each with a suggested send window (most dates recommend sending 2-4 days ahead of the date itself).
Selecting a date pre-fills a campaign draft with a suggested message tone and the [SITE_LINK] token already inserted, which staff or the shop owner can edit before sending.

Each seasonal date shows a small note on typical customer behaviour, for example Mother's Day and Valentine's Day both see a strong shift toward booked collection/delivery slots rather than same-day ordering, which is worth pairing with [[pre-orders-how-they-work|Pre-Orders]] rather than relying purely on walk-in demand.
A shop can dismiss a suggested date entirely if it's not relevant to their trade (a dry-January-themed date for an alcohol-forward menu, for instance).

blocks.caption: Seasonal Planner showing upcoming key dates with suggested send windows, including Valentine's Day highlighted three days out.

blocks.text: Combining tools for a bigger date

For genuinely high-demand dates, shops often combine a seasonal SMS send with a short-window discount rather than relying on the SMS alone, and some run a temporary points boost through [[mkt-loyalty-points|Loyalty Points]] at the same time to encourage repeat custom in the days immediately after the peak date, when trade often dips as a natural comedown from a busy event.

A downtime-style discount can also be scheduled specifically around a seasonal date rather than a recurring weekly window, see [[mkt-downtime-promotions|the Downtime Promotions article]] for the mechanics, the promotion setup is identical, it's simply given a single-occurrence end date rather than a recurring weekly schedule.
Timing considerations

items: The standard 7-day gap between campaigns still applies, so a shop planning both a mid-month promotion and a seasonal send needs to plan the calendar rather than assume both can go out independently.
Big football fixture nights are flagged with shorter lead times (same day to 24 hours) since demand builds quickly and unpredictably around kick-off rather than days in advance.
Bank holiday Mondays are flagged separately from the surrounding weekend, since ordering patterns on the holiday itself often resemble a Sunday rather than a typical Monday.

blocks.text: Troubleshooting

"We missed the suggested send window for Christmas", a shop can still send a campaign manually outside the Seasonal Planner's suggestion, the planner is guidance rather than a hard restriction, though sending very close to or on the date itself typically performs worse since most customers have already decided where to order from.

"Our seasonal campaign didn't send at the scheduled time", check the shop hasn't already used its send for the 7-day window on an unrelated campaign, the platform-wide send-frequency limit still applies to seasonal sends and will silently queue the campaign for the next eligible date rather than sending it immediately.

"Can we request more than the usual two per-year exception sends around Christmas specifically?", this needs a support ticket to Account Management the same as any other exception request, Christmas isn't treated differently from other high-demand dates in terms of the annual exception cap.

"The suggested message for a date doesn't fit our shop", the suggested wording is a starting draft, not a fixed template, shops are free to rewrite it entirely before sending, character limits and formatting rules are the only constraints carried over from the standard campaign composer.
Overview

Every shop receives a monthly statement covering their FMO charges, the flat subscription described in [[sales-subscription-commission|the subscription and commission article]], plus any variable charges incurred that month such as same-day transfer fees or SMS usage above the free allowance. This article covers how that statement is put together, how VAT is applied, and where to find historical invoices.
What's on a monthly statement

items: The flat monthly subscription fee for the billing period.

Any same-day transfer fees incurred that month, itemised per transfer with the date and reference (see [[sales-getting-paid-timelines|Getting Paid: Bank Transfer Timelines]] for how these fees are charged).
SMS usage charges beyond the shop's free monthly allowance, itemised as a single line total rather than per message.
Card processing pass-through fees for online payments, shown separately from FMO's own charges since these are collected on behalf of the payment provider, not FMO itself.

blocks.text: How VAT is applied

VAT-registered shops have their VAT number recorded against the account (added or updated via Account > Shop Details in the Partner App, the same self-service area covered in [[sales-updating-shop-details|the account details article]]), and the subscription and any variable fees are charged with VAT added at the standard UK rate. Shops that aren't VAT-registered are charged the same underlying amount with no VAT line added, since there's nothing to charge VAT on in that case.

The 3% minimum customer discount and FMO's 0% commission model don't themselves attract separate VAT treatment on the statement, they affect the value of the order the shop is paid out on, not a charge FMO levies on the shop, so they don't appear as a billing line in the way the subscription does.

blocks.caption: Monthly statement PDF showing the subscription line, itemised same-day transfer fees, SMS overage charge, and VAT applied at the standard rate.

blocks.text: Finding and downloading statements

Statements are generated automatically on the 1st of each month covering the prior calendar month, and are available as a downloadable PDF under Accounts > Billing > Statements, going back to the account's original sign-up date. Shops running more than one site under a group arrangement receive a single consolidated statement rather than one per shop, see [[sales-multi-site-accounts|the Multi-Site Accounts article]] for how billing is combined in that setup.
Troubleshooting

"Our statement shows VAT but we're not VAT-registered", check whether a VAT number was accidentally entered under Account > Shop Details, sometimes copied in error from a previous accountant's template; removing it corrects future statements, but a statement already issued needs a manual credit note raised via Accounts rather than being edited directly.

"We think we've been charged commission somewhere on this statement", walk the shop through each line item individually, referencing [[sales-subscription-commission|the subscription and commission article]] if needed, what's often mistaken for commission is the card processing pass-through fee, which is a separate provider charge, not an FMO commission.

"Can we get a statement broken down by site even though we're billed as one group?", yes, a per-site cost breakdown is available on request from Accounts even though the invoice itself is consolidated, this is common for multi-site owners who need to allocate costs internally between locations.

"We need last year's statements for a tax return and can't find them", statements older than 12 months roll off the default Accounts > Billing > Statements view but are never deleted, use the date range filter at the top of the screen or, failing that, request a resend from Accounts with the specific months needed.
Overview

A multi-site account is how FMO handles an owner running more than one shop, whether that's two branches of the same takeaway or a small group of differently branded sites. Rather than treating each shop as a completely separate, unconnected FMO account, a multi-site setup links them under one owner-level login while keeping each shop's day-to-day operation independent.

This is set up during onboarding for a group signing up multiple shops at once, following broadly the same process described in [[sales-signing-up-new-shop|Signing Up a New Shop]], or added later when an existing single-site shop owner opens a second location, in which case Accounts links the new shop to the existing owner record rather than creating an entirely fresh, unrelated account.
What's shared and what's per-site

items: Owner login and staff permissions are managed at the group level, see [[acc-multi-user-access|Multi-User Access]] for how individual staff logins and permission levels work across sites.
Billing is consolidated into a single monthly statement rather than one per shop, covered in [[sales-vat-invoicing|the VAT & Invoicing article]].

Each shop retains its own AP Funds balance, Smart Link terminal, menu, opening hours, and delivery zone, these are never merged or shared across sites, a driver assigned at one shop has no visibility of another site's orders.

Marketing tools (SMS campaigns, Loyalty Points, Downtime Promotions) can be configured per-site individually, or pushed identically to every linked shop at once from the group-level Marketing dashboard, whichever suits the owner's operation.

blocks.caption: Group-level dashboard showing three linked shops, each with its own AP Funds balance and Smart Link status, under a single owner login.

blocks.text: Adding or removing a site

Adding a new site to an existing group account still requires the new shop to go through its own full verification and terminal shipping process, exactly as a standalone shop would, a multi-site relationship doesn't skip any onboarding step, it simply links the resulting accounts together once each is live.

Removing a site from a group (a closure, or a sale of one location while keeping others) is treated the same as any ownership or account change and must go through Sales & Accounts, following the same principle set out in [[sales-updating-shop-details|Account Details: Updating Shop Information]] for ownership changes on a single site, it isn't something an owner can unlink themselves in-app.
Pricing for multiple sites

Multi-site subscriptions are quoted individually by the Accounts team rather than being a fixed multiple of the standard single-site fee, groups of three or more shops typically see a modest per-site discount compared to the standalone rate, but this is confirmed case by case rather than published as a flat table.
Troubleshooting

"An owner says they can only see one of their two shops when they log in", check whether the second shop was actually linked to the same owner record during onboarding, occasionally a second site is set up as a fully separate account by mistake, if so this needs correcting by Accounts rather than attempted as a permissions fix.

"Can AP Funds be moved between two of an owner's shops?", no, each site's AP Funds balance is entirely separate and reflects that specific shop's own online takings, there's no internal transfer mechanism between sites even under a shared owner login.

"We want one SMS campaign to go out from both our shops at once", this can be done from the group-level Marketing dashboard by selecting multiple sites when building the campaign, but each site's own send-frequency limit and customer segment still applies individually, it isn't treated as one combined audience.

"A staff member who works across both our shops needs access to each", set this up under Multi-User Access at the group level rather than creating two separate staff logins, a single staff account can be granted access to specific sites individually.

Drivers occasionally report that the Driver App has crashed, frozen, or become unresponsive mid-shift, most commonly while trying to mark an order as departed or delivered. This is disruptive for both the driver and the shop, since [[hw-smart-link-tracking-drivers|driver tracking on Smart Link]] and the automatic customer delivery notifications both depend on status updates actually reaching the app in real time. Work through the checklist below before assuming a platform-side fault, the large majority of these cases trace back to the driver's own device rather than the app itself.
Step-by-step diagnosis

items: Ask the driver which device and OS version they're using, the Driver App requires Android 9 or later, or iOS 14 or later, an older unsupported device is by far the most common cause of repeated crashes.

Check the app version under the driver's profile menu (three-line menu > About), and ask them to update from their device's app store if it isn't current, a build more than two versions behind can miss recent stability fixes.

Ask the driver how much free storage their phone has, background location tracking and turn-by-turn navigation both need working memory, a phone reporting under roughly 500MB free storage is a strong candidate for repeated app crashes under load.

Have the driver force-close the app fully (not just backgrounding it) and reopen it, rather than restarting their phone first, this resolves the majority of one-off freezes without losing their current shift login.
If it happens again shortly after reopening, have the driver restart the phone itself, this clears a wider range of memory and background-process issues than closing the app alone.

blocks.caption: Driver App crash report screen showing the option to send a diagnostic log, along with the device model, OS version, and app build number.

blocks.text: Sending a diagnostic log

If the crash repeats after a restart, ask the driver to reopen the app and use Help > Send Diagnostic Log, this captures the recent crash detail and device information without the driver needing to describe it themselves, and is the fastest route to a useful ticket if this needs escalating further.
What to tell the driver and shop

Reassure the driver that an app crash doesn't lose their assigned deliveries, order and driver status are held server-side, so once the app reopens and reconnects, their current jobs reappear correctly. Advise the shop that if a driver's status looks stuck on the tracking screen because of an app crash, staff can manually mark the order Delivered from Smart Link once the driver confirms completion by phone, exactly as covered for a stale GPS fix in the driver tracking article.
Escalation
Most single-driver crash reports resolve with an update, a restart, or freeing up storage, and don't need escalating beyond logging the diagnostic report. Escalate in the cases below.

items: If several drivers report crashing on the same app version within a short window regardless of device, escalate to the Platform team immediately with the affected app version, this points to a release-side bug rather than individual device issues.

If a crash has affected a driver's recorded deliveries in a way that could impact their pay calculation, escalate to the team responsible for [[del-driver-pay|Driver Pay]] with the affected order references so earnings can be checked and corrected manually rather than left to self-resolve.

If a driver reports the app crashing specifically and repeatedly on a device that meets the minimum OS requirement, escalate to Platform with the diagnostic log reference rather than continuing to troubleshoot the same steps on a call.

blocks.text: Overview

A customer or shop occasionally reports that the price shown for an item on the customer-facing app or site doesn't match what shows on the Smart Link terminal, or what the shop actually charges. This is nearly always a sync timing issue between where a price change is made and where it's displayed, rather than the two systems genuinely disagreeing on the price on file. Establishing which price is actually correct on the shop's own record is the first step in every case of this type.
Step-by-step diagnosis

items: Check the item's current price in the shop's Menu Editor (Settings > Menu > Editor, distinct from the live-toggle screen covered in [[menu-availability|Menu Availability]]), this is the source of truth for what the price should be right now.

Compare the timestamp of the most recent price change against when the customer or shop reports seeing the mismatch, a change made moments before an order was placed can take up to a couple of minutes to reach the customer-facing site in rare cases, even though most availability and price syncs land within seconds.

Ask the shop to force a manual sync from Settings > Account > Sync Now on the terminal itself, the same fix used for a stale menu or shop name shown in [[hw-smart-link-getting-started|the Getting Started article]]'s common issues section, this resolves the majority of terminal-side mismatches immediately.

Check whether the customer's device is showing a cached version of the menu, for example a browser tab left open from earlier in the day, ask them to refresh or reopen the app rather than assuming the platform itself is wrong.

Confirm the order was actually charged at the correct current price in Payments > Transaction History, since a mismatch in what's displayed doesn't always mean the customer was actually charged incorrectly.

blocks.caption: Menu Editor showing an item's price history log, with the most recent change timestamp highlighted against the current live price.

blocks.text: Common causes

items: A staff member changed a price on one device (for example a back-office laptop) moments before another staff member looked at the terminal, which hadn't yet pulled the update.
The same dish exists under two menu listings, similar to the duplicate-category issue covered for availability toggles, and only one listing's price was updated.

A scheduled price change (for a limited-time menu or event pricing) took effect at a different time than the shop expected, worth checking the item's Advanced Availability and pricing schedule rather than assuming the base price is simply wrong.

The terminal itself is on an older firmware build with a known sync delay, see [[hw-smart-link-firmware-updates|Managing Firmware Updates]] for how to check the current build and whether an update is overdue.

blocks.text: What to tell the customer

If the customer was charged the correct current price despite seeing an old one displayed briefly, reassure them the charge itself is accurate and the display issue has been raised with the shop. If they were genuinely overcharged against the price shown at the time they ordered, this should be corrected as a manual adjustment via Payments > Adjustments rather than left for the shop to resolve informally.
Escalation
Most price mismatches resolve with a manual Sync Now and don't need escalating further, especially once confirmed as a timing issue rather than a genuine data discrepancy.

items: If Sync Now doesn't resolve the mismatch after two attempts several minutes apart, check [[hw-smart-link-connectivity|connectivity]] first, a terminal with a degraded connection may accept the Sync Now tap but fail to actually pull the update.

If the mismatch persists after connectivity and a fresh sync are both confirmed fine, escalate to the Platform team with the item name, both prices observed, and timestamps, this may indicate a genuine data sync fault rather than a timing delay.
If multiple shops report the same class of mismatch around the same time, escalate immediately as a possible wider sync issue rather than treating each shop's ticket individually.
